<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/understanding-administrator-management-settings-business-insights","lastmod":"2024-11-13T05:28Z","nid":"1473136"} -->
## Understanding Administrator Management Settings in Business Insights

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/understanding-administrator-management-settings-business-insights
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Authentication & Administration > Administrator and Role Management > Understanding Administrator Management Settings in Business Insights
- Last modified: 2024-11-13T05:28Z
- Summary: Information on password and SAML authentication settings for admins in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

On the Administrator Management page (Administration > Administrator Management > Administrator Management), you can configure password expiration, SAML authentication, and other settings for admins.

If you are subscribed to the Authentication Service service, the Administrator Management page shows a link to the Authentication Service Admin Portal. You can manage your admins from the [Authentication Service Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/accessing-and-navigating-zidentity-admin-portal). To learn more, see [What Is Authentication Service?](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/what-zidentity)
See image.

## Password Management

If you're using the Zscaler-hosted admin database to authenticate admins, you can enable password expiration for all admins logging in to the Business Insights Admin Portal. To learn more, see [Configuring Password Expiration](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/configuring-password-expiration-business-insights).

## SAML Authentication for Administrators

Admins can be authenticated via SAML using an external admin database rather than the admin database in the Business Insights Admin Portal. The Zscaler service supports identity provider (IdP)-initiated SAML to authenticate admins. You can integrate admin authentication with your existing two-factor authentication solution. The Zscaler service supports SAML 2.0 and later. To learn more, see [Configuring SAML for Admins](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/configuring-saml-admins-business-insights).

The Zscaler service doesn't enforce password expiration for external admin databases using SAML.

## Advanced Configuration

You can choose the action to be taken on admins when their linked user accounts are deleted using the System for Cross-Domain Identity Management (SCIM) protocol. You can allow SCIM to delete the admin and its linked user account, or prevent SCIM from deleting it. To learn more, see [Configuring Advanced Configuration for Admins](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/configuring-advanced-configuration-admins).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-architecture","lastmod":"2024-08-29T23:44Z","nid":"1473081"} -->
## Understanding Business Insights Architecture

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-architecture
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Getting Started > Understanding Business Insights Architecture
- Last modified: 2024-08-29T23:44Z
- Summary: Information about Business Insights architecture.

Business Insights provides intuitive visualization and reporting metrics for your SaaS app usage and workplace-related data in a centralized [Business Insights Admin Portal](https://admin.zscaleranalytics.net/) that helps with:

- Cost reduction and savings across SaaS apps by downsizing underutilized licenses and overlapping apps.
- Driving return to office strategy and analyzing office utilization metrics and their pattern of usage, whether hybrid or remote, for efficient workplace management.

To set up and view Business Insights for your organization, you must consider the following prerequisites:

- To gain SaaS app insights, you must be subscribed to the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service.
- To gain workplace insights, in addition to the ZIA service, you must have Zscaler Client Connector deployed on all relevant endpoints you want to track for office utilization.

## Business Insights Architecture

Business Insights receives signals and data from 4 data sources: the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service that acts as one of the input feeders, identity providers (IdPs) like Okta and Entra ID, SaaS application connector integrations (supported for apps such as Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google, and GitHub), and [custom application signatures](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-application-configuration). Zscaler's direct connector integration to view business insights overextends other data source functionalities. However, Business Insights provides metrics even when integration into a specific app is not available with the help of other data sources.

Business Insights can differentiate between your subscribed apps vs. used apps by populating metadata fields that show subscription details, such as cost, license plans, contract start dates, end dates, etc. All of these fields can be filtered to present a report of representative apps. At the same time, Business Insights also presents the app usage and workplace data by analyzing your ZIA traffic, identity provider (login data), or API integrations (direct app connectors) to help you save business costs.

Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps. By default, only a subset of these apps are shown in the portal, depending on your business relevance, to help streamline your experience and avoid unnecessary information. To learn more, see [What Is Zscaler Business Insights?](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/what-zscaler-business-insights)

[Image: Business Insights Architecture]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-terminology","lastmod":"2025-08-06T23:32Z","nid":"1473086"} -->
## Understanding Business Insights Terminology

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-terminology
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Getting Started > Understanding Business Insights Terminology
- Last modified: 2025-08-06T23:32Z
- Summary: Information about the terms used in Business Insights.

This article lists Business Insights terms and their definitions to help you understand and interpret the metrics with the intended context and perspective.

## Application Insights Terms

The following terms apply to Application Insights:

- **Active Users**: The number of active users for an app in the last 30 days. Active users have accessed or used the app at least once in the last 30 days.
- **Application Connector**: An application connector integrates with the SaaS provider to collect license and usage information for the app. Configuring a connector involves providing information to call the provider's APIs. To learn more, see [Onboarding SaaS Apps for Business Insights](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/onboarding-saas-apps-business-insights).
- **Supported Apps**: Application connectors for supported apps can be configured in the Business Insights Admin Portal. With a connector configured, the insights for an app are more detailed. Currently, Business Insights supports connector integration for Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google, and GitHub.
- **Purchased Seats**: The number of seats purchased within a subscription plan. One seat is assigned to one user.
- **Assigned Seats**: The number of seats assigned to users from the purchased seats.
- **Data Source**: The source from where the application usage is discovered. Business Insights receives signals and data from 4 data sources: the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service that acts as one of the input feeders, identity providers (IdPs) like Okta and Entra ID, SaaS application connector integrations (supported for apps such as Okta, M365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Box, Google, and GitHub), and [custom application signatures](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-application-configuration).
- **Discovered Apps**: Apps whose usage is discovered within your organization's traffic. Zscaler can discover the usage of over 30K apps.
- **Engagement Index**: This metric shows the application's engagement percentage. This calculation varies based on the following metadata availability:
  - Without [Plan Details](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-application-details#plan): The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days for an app. For example, suppose you have 50 active users in the last 30 days and 100 in the last 90 days for Box. In that case, the engagement index is calculated by dividing the number of active users in the last 30 days by the number of active users in the last 90 days, and multiplying it by 100 (i.e., [50÷100]×100 = 50%).
  - With [Plan Details](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-application-details#plan): The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the number of purchased seats for an app. For example, suppose you have 50 active users in the last 30 days and 100 purchased seats for Box. In that case, the engagement index is calculated by dividing the number of active users in the last 30 days by the number of purchased seats, and multiplying it by 100 (i.e., [50÷100]×100 = 50%). If the data of the purchased seats is unavailable, the service replaces it with the number of assigned seats. If both the data are unavailable, the service defaults to the preceding calculation performed for apps without plan details. If multiple plans exist, the service shows the data for the plan with the lowest engagement index.
- **Growth Trend**: The percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days. For example, if you have 50 active users in the last 30 days but 100 active users before the last 30 days, the growth trend is calculated by dividing the increase or decrease in the number of active users by the number of active users before the last 30 days, and multiplying it by 100 ([100−50]÷100×100 = decrease of 50%).
- **Capability**: An app capability is the service that it provides for its users. For example, **Video Conferencing**is a capability provided by Zoom and Webex.
- **Overlapping Apps**: Users using multiple apps with similar capabilities. For example, the usage of Slack and Microsoft Teams within your organization that have similar capabilities.
- **High Usage Apps:** Apps with over 80% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.
- **Low Usage Apps:** Apps with less than 30% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.

## Workplace Insights Terms

The following terms apply to Workplace Insights:

- **Workplaces**: An organization's traffic ingress and egress points. There are two types of workplaces:
  - **Inferred Locations**: These are individual [ZIA locations](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-locations) configured in the ZIA Admin Portal (a ZIA location can also consist of sub-locations) and inferred IP addresses that the Business Insights service concludes as the organization's workplace based on the amount of traffic, the number of users behind the IP address, and more assuring metrics.
  - **Configured Offices**: These are the grouping of inferred locations into a configured office with metadata. To learn more, see [About Configured Offices](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-configured-offices).
- **Assigned Headcount**: The number of users assigned to an office.
- **Capacity**: The number of employees the office can accommodate.
- **Average Attendance**: The average attendance for an office site is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplace by the total number of assigned headcount for the workplace, then multiplying it by 100.
- **Average Occupancy**: The average occupancy for a workplace is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplace by the site capacity, then multiplying it by 100.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Uploading Application Contracts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/uploading-application-contracts
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Application Insights > Uploading Application Contracts
- Last modified: 2025-06-12T23:55Z
- Summary: How to upload application contracts in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

The article explains how to upload contracts in the Business Insights Admin Portal to view their insights.

To upload a contract:

1. Go to **Applications** > **All Contracts** > **Upload Contracts**. The **Upload Contracts** window appears.
2. Click **Upload Files**. You can upload multiple files in one attempt. The Business Insights service supports PDF, DOC, and XLS files. See image.
3. Locate the contract file in your system.
4. Select the files and click **Open**. The file is uploaded successfully and moved to the [Processing Queue](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-processing-queue) page where the file is parsed for necessary metadata. You can go to the Processing Queue page to view its status. Depending on the size and number of files, the data is processed within minutes, hours, or days. After the file is successfully processed, the contract information is available in the All Contracts table on the [All Contracts](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-contracts) page.

[Image: Upload Files]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/using-tables-business-insights","lastmod":"2024-02-16T06:28Z","nid":"1473126"} -->
## Using Tables in Business Insights

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/using-tables-business-insights
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Getting Started > Admin Portal > Using Tables in Business Insights
- Last modified: 2024-02-16T06:28Z
- Summary: How to use tables in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/loose.dtd"

Data in the Business Insights Admin Portal is organized and displayed in tables. You can modify the default settings for each table. Every time you make a change, the settings are stored in your browser's local storage so that your changes are preserved the next time you log in.

If you clear your cache or use a different browser, your settings are lost.

You can do the following:

- Reorder columns
- Resize columns
- Hide columns
- Sort the column data
- Reset table to default settings

You can reorder columns in one of two ways:

- From the Table
- From the Column Menu settings

When you hover over a column header in the table, a **Move** cursor appears. To reorder the column, drag and drop it to the desired location. An arrow indicates where the column is placed. The table refreshes and displays data in the new column order.

The column menu settings also change to reflect the new order.

[Image: reorder column in Business Insights tables]

When you hover over a listed column name in the settings, a **Move** cursor appears. Drag and drop the column name to the desired position. The table refreshes and displays the data in the new column order.

[Image: Screenshot of reordering columns from Zscaler table column menu settings]

When the data in a column takes up more space than the viewing area allows, it is truncated. You can view the truncated data in the tooltip. You can also increase the column width.

To increase the column width, hover over the right border of the column. A **Resize** icon appears. Adjust the column to the desired width.

[Image: Screenshot of resizing columns for Zscaler tables]

When you do not need to view all the columns at the same time, you can hide them so only the columns you want to view are visible.

To hide a column, hover over the **Column Menu** or **Gear** icon on the top right of the table, and uncheck the column names you want to hide. The table refreshes and displays only the checked columns.

For tables under **Administration**pages, you must have at least one column visible at all times.

[Image: Screenshot of hiding columns for Zscaler tables]

Some columns have a sort icon indicating that you can sort the data in those columns. You can sort data in ascending or descending order.

To sort a column, click on the sort icon in the table column header.

[Image: Sort the coulmn in RIsk360 Admin Portal]

When you make changes to the columns, you can go back to the default settings by hovering over the **Column Menu** and clicking the **Reset** icon.

This doesn't reset your sort order.

[Image: Screenshot of Reset icon for Zscaler tables]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/using-zscaler-help-browser","lastmod":"2025-08-06T23:32Z","nid":"1480196"} -->
## Using the Zscaler Help Browser

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/using-zscaler-help-browser
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Getting Started > Admin Portal > Using the Zscaler Help Browser
- Last modified: 2025-08-06T23:32Z
- Summary: Accessing and using the the Zscaler Help Browser within the Business Insights Admin Portal.

The Zscaler Help Browser is available for all pages within the Business Insights Admin Portal. Through the Help Browser you can view Zscaler Help Portal articles in context with the page you're on, without leaving the Business Insights Admin Portal.

To open the Help Browser:

1. Go to the page where you want to view an article.
2. Click the **Open Help Browser** icon in the lower-right corner. See image.

The Help Browser displays the article and any video relevant to the page you're viewing
See image.

## About the Help Browser

The Help Browser is also adjustable. There are different features to help you customize the browser and navigate within it.

### Customizing the Help Browser

You can do the following to customize the Help Browser:

- Move the Help Browser
- Resize the Help Browser
- Change the font size

Zscaler saves your customization until you log out or the session expires.

### Navigating within the Help Browser

You can do the following to navigate within the Help Browser:

1. View the article relevant to the page you're viewing in the Business Insights Admin Portal.
2. Navigate back and forth across articles you've viewed.
3. Search for an article.
4. Copy the URL of an article.
5. Close the Help Browser.
6. Open the article in new browser tab.

[Image: Screenshot of the Help Browser and its features]

Closing the Help Browser clears your navigation history. When you reopen the browser, it displays the article relevant to the page you are viewing, and you are unable to navigate back and forth to articles you've viewed in the previous Help Browser session.

[Image: Screenshot highlighting the Help Browser icon.]

**[Image: Screenshot showing the Help Browser window with the relevant article and help]**

You can move the Help Browser anywhere within the menu bar and footer. When you hover over the browser header, a **Move** cursor appears. Click and drag the Help Browser to the desired location.

**[Image: Screenshot showing how to move the Help Browser]**

You can resize the Help Browser to expand videos, pictures, and content. When you hover to the top-left corner of the browser, an **Expand** cursor appears. Click and drag the corner to resize the window.

**[Image: Screenshot showing how to resize the Help Browser]**

There are different font sizes for the Help Browser. You can click the **Font** icons to increase or decrease the text size.

**[Image: Screenshot showing the Font icons in the Help Browser]**
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/viewing-application-details","lastmod":"2025-06-12T23:30Z","nid":"1473196"} -->
## Viewing Application Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-application-details
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Application Insights > Viewing Application Details
- Last modified: 2025-06-12T23:30Z
- Summary: Information about the application details page in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

The Application Details page (Application > Inventory > click on the application) provides a complete analysis and metrics for the application that is currently being used within your organization. You can view the engagement index, active and inactive user data, application plan details, licensing insights, and risk and compliance data, among other metrics.

See image.

The page contains an overview section and the following tabs:

- Overview Section
- Engagement Index & Users Tab
- Contracts Tab
- Licensing Insights Tab
- Risk & Compliance Tab

In the **Overview**section, you can view:

- **Summary**: A brief description of the application.
- **Capability**: The various capabilities offered by the application. For example, Okta's capabilities include identity management, access control, two-factor authentication, etc.
- **Alternatives**: A list of alternative applications with similar capabilities.
- **Website**: The official website for the application.
- **Status**: The connection status between Business Insights and the application (i.e., whether the application is onboarded to Business Insights or not). For connector-integrated apps, the application connector's API connection is valid or expired.
- **Data Source**: The source from where the application usage is discovered (i.e., identity provider (IdP), Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), by connector integration, or custom application signature such as **IDP**, **ZIA**, **CONNECTOR**,or**CUSTOM ZIA**).
- **Sanction Status**: Whether the application's use is sanctioned or not in your organization.
- **Risk Index**: The risk index assigned to the application. This setting for the app is configured in the ZIA Admin Portal. To learn more, see [About Cloud Applications](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-cloud-applications) and [About Shadow IT Report](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-shadow-it-report).
- **Tags**: The tags linked to the application. To learn more, see [About Application Tags](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-application-tags).

The top-right of the page displays the **Delete**or **Connect**option based on whether the application is connected for Business Insights computation or not. To remove the app connection, click **Delete**. Click **Connect** to go to the [Add Applications](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/onboarding-saas-apps-business-insights) page, where you can configure a connector for the app. These options are available for connector-supported apps only.

See image.

On the **Engagement Index & Users**tab, you can view:

## Active and Inactive Users Graph

This graph shows the active vs. inactive user trend for the number of purchased license seats. Hover over a date on the graph to view the engagement index, number of purchased seats, and the number of active and inactive users along with their percentage increase or decrease. You can filter this tab for information for the last 30 days or 12 months.

See image.

## Users Table

The top of the **Users**table shows the number of purchased seats, assigned seats. Use the following operators to filter the table:

- Select the time frame for viewing the data from the last 30, 60, or 90 days (last month, 2 months, or 3 months for the ZIA table).
- Switch to view data from the tabs between**Active Users** or **Inactive Users**. By default, **Active Users** is selected.
- Search for a specific user in the table.
- Click **Export** to download the data for the preceding filters into a CSV file.

The table shows the top 100 records by user activity.

See image.

Depending on the application's data source—how the application usage is discovered within your organization (**IDP** or **ZIA**), if you have a connector configured with a [supported app](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-terminology#supported-app) (**CONNECTOR**), or if you have a custom application signature configured (**CUSTOM ZIA**) —one of the following Users tables appears:

- For ZIA Discovered or CUSTOM ZIA Apps
- For IDP Discovered Apps
- For CONNECTOR Apps

If you're viewing application details for Microsoft 365, the User field shows obfuscated data by default. To view usernames, enable the setting in the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://admin.microsoft.com/). To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-US/microsoft-365/troubleshoot/miscellaneous/reports-show-anonymous-user-name).

- **User**: The name of the user.
- **Email**: The user's email ID.
- **Department**: The department the user belongs to.
- **Total Bytes**: The total upload and download bytes by the user for the app.
- **Upload Bytes:** The total upload bytes by the user.
- **Download Bytes**: The total download bytes by the user.
- **No. of Transactions**: The number of transactions by the user for the application.
- **Last Active**: The date when the user last used the application.

See image.

- **User**: The name of the user.
- **Email**: The user's email ID.
- **Department**: The department the user belongs to.

See image.

- **Email**: The user's email ID.
- **Department**: The department the user belongs to.
- **License Type**: The license type of the application that is assigned to the user. For example, Microsoft 365 offers enterprise plans such as E1, E3, E5, etc. based on customer requirements.
- **Last Active**: The date when the user last used the application.

See image.

## Contracts Table

The **Contracts**table shows the list of contracts your organization is subscribed to for the application. For each contract, you can view:

- **Contract**: The name of the contract.
- **Item Name**: The name of the service in the contract.
- **End Date**: The end date of the application subscription.
- **Licensing Model**: The licensing model for the subscription (e.g., Per User, Per GB).
- **Quantity**: The number of users or GB of data opted in the subscription.
- **List Price**: The total price of the license.
- **Annual Price**: The annual price of the license.

Use the filter option to filter the table data. Click the **Add** icon to show or hide the filter options. Use the filter-based range icons for precise data filtration (i.e., greater than, less than, between, ends with, equal to, not equal to). Click a contract to see more information about it in the [Contracts drawer](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-contract-details).

See image.

The **Licensing Insights** tab consists of a License Usage Funnel graph that shows the metrics for the license usage of the application. These metrics provide an understanding of the current license posture and help you manage them efficiently. You can view:

- **Purchased Seats**: The number of purchased seats for the application. The graph is split between different SKUs that you purchased for the application. Hover over the bar to view the number of purchased seats for each SKU.
- **Assigned Seats**: The number of seats assigned to users from the purchased seats. Hover over the bar to view the number of assigned seats for each SKU. This information is only applicable for connector-based datasource.
- **Active Users (Last 90 days)**: The number of active users for the assigned seats. Hover over the bar to view the number of active users for each plan.

You can filter this graph based on the data sources from the **Datasource** drop-down menu, or switch it between **Plans**and **Contract**views.

You can also select or deselect the line items you want to compare in the chart.

See image.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/viewing-application-overlap-details","lastmod":"2025-09-29T23:17Z","nid":"1473231"} -->
## Viewing Application Overlap Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-application-overlap-details
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Application Insights > Viewing Application Overlap Details
- Last modified: 2025-09-29T23:17Z
- Summary: Information on application comparison based on their capability in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

The Application Overlap Details page (Application > Overlapping Apps > click on the application) provides metrics for applications for a specific capability. You can view the user activity, overlap metrics, and app comparisons for a capability.

See image.

You can compare the overlap metrics for up to 4 apps at a time by using the drop-down menu in the upper-left of the page. After you select the apps for comparison, click **Apply**. The page is updated with the apps you selected.

The page contains the following sections:

## User Activity

The User Activity graph shows the weekly active user trend for each application. Hover over a date in the graph to view the number of active users for each app.

See image.

## Application Comparison

This table compares the apps in terms of engagement index, growth trend, etc. For each app, you can view:

- **Application**: The name of the application along with its logo.
- **Website**: The application's website.
- **Description**: The description of the application.
- **Data Source**: The source from where the application usage is discovered (i.e., identity provider (IdP), Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), by connector integration, or custom application signature such as **IDP**, **ZIA**, **CONNECTOR**,or**CUSTOM ZIA**).
- **Active Users**: The number of active users for the app.
- **Growth Trend**: The percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days. For example, if you have 50 active users in the last 30 days but 100 active users before the last 30 days, the growth trend is calculated by dividing the increase or decrease in the number of active users by the number of active users before the last 30 days, and multiplying it by 100 ([100−50]÷100×100 = decrease of 50%).
- **Engagement Index**: The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days for an app. For example, if you have 50 active users in the last 30 days and 100 in the last 90 days for Box, the engagement index is calculated by dividing the number of active users in the last 30 days by the number of active users in the last 90 days, and multiplying it by 100 (i.e., [50÷100]×100 = 50%).
- **Top 5 Departments**: The top 5 departments by app usage.
- **Spend**: The amount spent (in US Dollars) by the organization on the app subscription.
- **Contract Date**: The date when the app subscription ends.

See image.

[Image: The Overlap Details Page]

[Image: User Activity Section in the Overlap Details Page]

[Image: Application Comparision Section in the Overlap Details Page]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/viewing-contract-details","lastmod":"2025-07-07T22:19Z","nid":"1506921"} -->
## Viewing Contract Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-contract-details
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Application Insights > Viewing Contract Details
- Last modified: 2025-07-07T22:19Z
- Summary: How to view application contract details in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

The Contract Details drawer shows the licensing information, pricing, etc. for applications in the contracts. The top of the drawer shows the name of the contract, upcoming contract related deadlines, tags linked with the contract, and other important details (i.e., billing frequency, contacts, etc.).

To access the contract drawer, go to either:

- **Applications** > **All Contracts** > click on a contract
- The [Application Details](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-application-details) page > **Contracts** > click on a contract

## Overview

The Overview section shows the following information:

- **Start Date**: The contract start date.
- **End Date**: The contract end date
- **Annual Contract Value**: The annual contract value (ACV). The value is displayed as the default currency set on the [Contract Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/contract-settings) page. Click the **Edit** icon to update the currency.
- **Total Contract Value**: The total contract value (TCV). The value is displayed as the default currency set on the [Contract Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/contract-settings) page.
- **Payment Term**: The term of the payment agreed upon by both the parties (the vendor and your organization).
- **Payment Frequency**: The payment frequency for the contract (e.g., annual, quarterly).
- **Vendor**: The name of the vendor.
- **Seller**: The name of the seller.
- **Buyer**: The name of the contract buyer.
- **File**: The contract file uploaded to the Business Insights service. Click the **Download** icon to save the contract to your system, if available.

Click the **Column Menu**icon, then click the **Edit** icon to update any fields in the drawer and click **Save**. You can also click **Delete Contract** to remove the contract.

## Application Table

The application table shows the following information for each application in the contract:

- **Application**: The name of the application.
- **Item Name**: The name of the SKU subscribed to for the application.
- **End Date**: The date when the application subscription ends.
- **Licensing Model**: The licensing model for the application (i.e., **Per User**, **Per GB**, etc.).
- **Quantity**: The number of users or the GB of data subscribed to in the license.
- **List Price**: The price of the total licensing model.
- **Annual Price**: The annual price for the application subscription.
- **Start Date**: The subscription start date.
- **Discount**: The discount provided on the subscription.
- **Total**: The total price after discount.
- **Status**: The status of the application subscription (i.e, **Active**, **Expired**, or **Pending**). A pending status indicates that the subscription has not yet started.

Click the **Settings** icon to [modify the column data](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/using-tables-business-insights).

[Image: Contract Details drawer]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/viewing-offices-and-locations-chart","lastmod":"2025-08-06T23:32Z","nid":"1486606"} -->
## Viewing Offices and Locations in a Chart

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-offices-and-locations-chart
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Workplace Insights > Viewing Offices and Locations in a Chart
- Last modified: 2025-08-06T23:32Z
- Summary: Information on viewing the Offices and Locations page in a chart.

This article explains the data displayed on the Offices and Locations page (Workplace > Offices and Locations > Charts) in the Chart view.

See image.

To understand the data in a list or chart, see [About Offices and Locations](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-offices-and-locations) or [Viewing Offices and Locations on a Map](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-offices-and-locations-map).

## Viewing Offices and Locations in a Chart

To analyze the data for a specific metric or time frame:

- **Export as PDF**: Download the data on the page as a PDF file.
- **Time Range**: View workplace insights for the last 7 days, a week, a month, or 3 months, then choose the week, month, or 3 months from the right pane. The data aggregation for the custom week, month, or quarter might take some time to process. See image.
- Filter the insights by:
  - **Name**: The name of the workplace. You can only select to view data for either the configured offices or inferred locations at one time.
  - **Departments**or**Divisions**: The department filter is available unless you have at least one department mapping to a division on the [Department Mapping](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-department-mapping) page.
    - **Departments**: The departments within your organization. This data is mapped from the ZIA Admin Portal SCIM. If the values are inaccurate, contact a ZIA admin.
    - **Divisions**: The division that maps related departments.
  - **Days**: Specific days from the filtered time frame. Enable **Custom Dates**to select custom dates to include or exclude from the insights. By default, Saturdays and Sundays are excluded from the metrics. See image.
  - **User Types**: The type of users or employees visiting your organization. Selecting this filter doesn't filter the data unless you have defined user types for your organization in Business Insights. To enable this filter, contact Zscaler Support.

The page contains the following information:

### Averages Section

This section contains the following widgets:

- **Average Occupancy**: The average occupancy in percentage and numbers for the filtered offices within the specified time frame. This is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplaces by overall workplace capacities for the time period specified, then multiplying it by 100. You can view the total number of visits vs. the total possible capacity. The total possible capacity is determined by multiplying the capacity for all selected offices by the number of official working days within the time frame selected. For example, if your capacity is 100 and there are 5 official working days, the possible capacity is 500. You can also view the percentage increase or decrease in occupancy vs. the previous period of the same time (e.g., Month over Month (MoM), Week over Week (WoW), or Quarter over Quarter (QoQ)).
- **Peak / Low Occupancy**: The peak and low occupancy percentage on a particular day and the number of office visits for the filtered workplaces within the specified time frame.
- **Average Attendance**: The average attendance for the workplaces within the specified time frame. This is calculated by dividing the total number of visits to the workplaces by the total number of assigned headcount for the workplaces, then multiplying it by 100. You can view the total number of visits vs. the total possible assigned headcount. The total possible assigned headcount is determined by multiplying the capacity for all selected offices by the number of official working days within the time frame selected. For example, if your capacity is 100 and there are 5 official working days, the possible assigned headcount is 500. You can also view the percentage increase or decrease in attendance vs. the previous period of the same time (e.g., Month over Month (MoM), Week over Week (WoW), or Quarter over Quarter (QoQ)).
- **Average Visit Span**: The average time spent in the workplaces.

You can only view data for either the configured offices or inferred locations at one time. The metrics are calculated considering a 5-day work week.

See image.

The metrics for inferred location-based workplaces are estimated as the Business Insights service doesn't have precise metadata to provide accurate insight. Hence, Zscaler recommends [configuring offices](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/configuring-offices) (providing metadata) for inferred location-based workplaces to view accurate insights.
See image.

### Occupancy Tab

This tab consists of the following sections:

The explanatory sentence at the top of sections is shown for the filtered time frame and not for the time frames it is compared with.

#### Occupancy by Day

The graph shows the occupancy comparison trend for the time frame specified. For example, if you filter the data for the current week, this graph shows the occupancy comparison with last week's data. You can:

- View the data in the graph in percentage or number of visits by selecting the respective options (i.e., **Percentage** or **Visits**).
- View the data for a specific time frame by selecting the checkboxes next to the graph (e.g., last week or current week).
- View the average occupancy for the office within the specified time frame, as well as the occupancy goal percentage (and the numerical value) configured for the office.
- Hover over a date in the graph to view the percentage increase or decrease in the occupancy and the average occupancy.

#### Occupancy by Day of the Week

This graph shows the occupancy percentage for each day of the week. This is calculated by dividing the number of visits to the workplaces on that day by the possible capacity of the workplaces, then multiplying it by 100. You can:

- View the data in the graph in percentage or number of visits by selecting the respective options (i.e., **Percentage** or **Visits**).
- View the data for a specific time frame by selecting the checkboxes at the bottom of the graph (e.g., last week vs. current week).

See image.

### Attendance Tab

This tab consists of the following sections:

The explanatory sentence at the top of sections is shown for the filtered time frame and not for the time frames it is compared with.

#### Attendance by Day

The graph shows the attendance comparison trend for the time frame specified. For example, if you filtered the data for the current week, this graph shows the attendance percentage comparison with last week's data. You can:

- View the data in the graph in percentage, number of visits, or days per week by selecting the respective options (i.e., **Percentage**, **Visits**, or **Days per Week**).
- View the data for a specific time frame by selecting the checkboxes next to the graph (e.g., last week vs. current week).
- View the average attendance for the office within the specified time frame, as well as the attendance goal percentage (and the numerical value) configured for the office.
- Hover over a date in the graph to view the percentage increase or decrease in attendance and the average attendance.

#### Attendance by Day of the Week

This graph shows the attendance percentage for each day of the week. This is calculated by dividing the number of visits to the workplaces on that day by the total number of possible assigned headcount of the workplaces, then multiplying it by 100. You can:

- View the data in the graph in percentage or number of visits by selecting the respective options (i.e., **Percentage** or **Visits**).
- View the data for a specific time frame by selecting the checkboxes at the bottom of the graph (e.g., last week vs. current week).

#### Attendance by Days per Week

The pie chart shows the percentage of users (and their count) who came to the workplaces less than a day to 7 days a week. The center of the pie chart shows the total number of users.

#### Attendance by Department

The bar chart shows the percentage of users coming into the workplace from the total number of assigned headcount for the workplace and the expected attendance for each department at the workplace. Select the **Show Unassigned Users** checkbox to view the data for users that are not assigned to a department.

See image.

[Image: The Chart View of the Offices and Locations Page]

[Image: Estimated Averages]

[Image: Time Range Filter]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Viewing Offices and Locations on a Map

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-offices-and-locations-map
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Workplace Insights > Viewing Offices and Locations on a Map
- Last modified: 2024-12-12T23:53Z
- Summary: Information on viewing the Offices and Locations page in a map view in the Business Insights Admin Portal.

This article explains the data displayed on the Offices and Locations page (Workplace > Offices and Locations > Map) in the Map view. Additionally, you can view the metrics on this page as a list or chart. To learn more, see [About Offices and Locations](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-offices-and-locations) or [Viewing Offices and Locations in a Chart](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/viewing-offices-and-locations-chart).

To analyze the data for a specific data type or time frame, use the following filters:

- **Export as PDF**: Download the data on the page as a PDF file.
- **Time Range**: View data for the last 7 days, a week, a month, or 3 months, then choose the week, month, or 3 months from the right pane. The data aggregation for the custom week, month, or quarter might take some time to process.
- **Type**: The type of workplace (**Offices** or **Inferred Locations**). For **Geolocation**, select the workplaces based on the type selected. Business Insights automatically assigns names for inferred location workplaces that are based on IP addresses and retains the name assigned in the ZIA Admin Portal for [ZIA location](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-locations)-based workplaces. You can only select to view data for either the configured offices or inferred locations at one time.
- **Days**: Specific days from the filtered time frame. Enable **Custom Dates**to select custom dates to include or exclude from the insights. By default, Saturdays and Sundays are excluded from the metrics. See image.
- **Departments**or**Divisions**: The department filter is available unless you have at least one department mapping to a division on the [Department Mapping](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/about-department-mapping) page.
  - **Departments**: The departments within your organization. This data is mapped from the ZIA Admin Portal SCIM. If the values are inaccurate, contact a ZIA admin.
  - **Divisions**: The division that maps related departments.
- **User Types**: The type of users visiting your organization. Selecting user types doesn't filter the data unless you have defined these user types for your organization in Business Insights. To enable this filter, contact Zscaler Support.
- Enable the **Show ZIA Sub-locations** toggle to view ZIA sub-locations in the list. This option is available when you filter the data for inferred location-based workplaces.

### Map View

Switch between **Geography** and **Remote User Density** to view the following insights:

- Geography
- Remote User Density

View the distribution of workplaces across the globe. You can zoom in and out using your mouse or the icons at the bottom-right corner. Click a workplace to view:

- The name of the workplace.
- The city, state or province, and country where the workplace is located.
- The type of workplace, whether a configured office or inferred location.
- **Average Attendance**: The average attendance for the workplace for the filtered time frame.
- **Average Occupancy**: The average occupancy for the workplace for the filtered time frame.
- **See Details**: Click to view additional details for the workplace. To learn more, see [Analyzing a Workplace](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/analyzing-workplace).

If you don't see a configured office on the map, metadata for that office is missing. Make sure you specify the city, state or province, and country information when configuring offices to locate the configured office on the map.

You can only select to view data for either the configured offices or inferred locations at one time.

See image.

View locations across the globe for remote users. Zoom in and out using your mouse or the icons at the bottom-right corner. You can view:

- The total number of remote users across the globe.
- **Potential Sites Opportunities**: A list of cities with the number and percentage of remote users where you can consider opening an office.
- The total number of remote users working from the country by hovering over a country.
- Countries with darker shade signify more remote users compared to lighter-shaded countries with fewer remote users.
- Workplaces that show the following information when you hover over them: Click on the workplace to view additional details. To learn more, see [Analyzing a Workplace](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/analyzing-workplace).
  - The name of the workplace.
  - The city, state or province, and country where the workplace is located.
  - The type of workplace, whether a configured office or inferred location.
  - **Average Attendance**: The average attendance for the workplace for the filtered time frame.
  - **Average Occupancy**: The average occupancy for the workplace for the filtered time frame.

See image.

[Image: Geography Tab in Map View]

[Image: Remote User DensityTab]

[Image: Days Filter]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/business-insights/what-zscaler-business-insights","lastmod":"2024-02-16T06:25Z","nid":"1473076"} -->
## What Is Zscaler Business Insights?

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/what-zscaler-business-insights
- Product: Business Insights
- Path: Business Insights Help > Getting Started > What Is Zscaler Business Insights?
- Last modified: 2024-02-16T06:25Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Business Insights.

Zscaler Business Insights provides 360-degree visibility into your organization's SaaS application usage and spending insights, along with workplace metrics to help you save money and manage your workplace efficiently.

## SaaS Application Management

Nowadays, organizations depend on multiple applications to complete their day-to-day operations. This results in an unconstrained number of applications being consumed, which makes the application landscape management difficult within an organization. The challenges include:

- The process of gathering metrics and reports from various cross-functional teams, such as Accounting, IT, and Vendor Management to build an understanding of your application usage can be time-consuming.
- The majority of the application metrics are manually entered into a spreadsheet and must be updated frequently.
- The users' application engagement metrics for an application must be gathered manually from the application, if available.

Business Insights serves as a centralized engagement interface for all your licensed applications, and eliminates all the preceding challenges by providing the necessary information to effectively manage and optimize your application landscape.

By analyzing your application usage trends with Business Insights, you're equipped with accurate data to renew the correct number of licenses required by your organization. For example, if an organization purchases more than the required number of Microsoft 365 licenses, the data for how many of the purchased licenses are actually being used can be analyzed with the help of Business Insights and, subsequently, reduce the number of licenses during the renewal process.

### Key Features and Benefits

The key features and benefits of Business Insights for your applications landscape are as follows:

- **Instant Discovery**: Configure your applications and start viewing their metrics instantly.
- **Engagement Data**: Glance into the application's engagement ratio, spending trends, saving opportunities, inactive user data, usage by department, etc.
- **Shadow IT**: View and calculate spending on Shadow IT applications purchased by departments or users within your organization.
- **SaaS Visibility**: Experience total visibility into your application landscape. View the list of all your applications in one place, including overlaps.
- **Cost Control**: Reduce unnecessary and redundant application expenses.

## Office Workplace & Workforce Management

Understanding office workplace utility helps you manage and control costs, ensure employee productivity, and maintain a seamless office experience. However, these insights can be hard to access, spread out across multiple departments and numerous standalone tools. Stringing together the data places enormous pressure on IT and other relevant teams. Business Insights provides a better way to access these insights and visualize the trends granularly. The HR and Workplace & Facilities leaders can conduct data-based office capacity planning and understand hour-by-hour office utilization down to department and employee levels.

### Key Features and Benefits

The key features and benefits of Business Insights for your office workplace utilization are as follows:

- **Workplace Insights**: Optimize office overheads with details on what days workers spend in the office vs. hybrid vs. remote, as well as which departments come into the office most frequently.
- **Cost Control**: Rich insights and predictive cost-saving models enable you to save money by optimizing workplace utilization.
- **Back-to-Office Strategy**: Leverage hour-by-hour office utilization data, and access weekly, monthly, and quarterly workplace usage data across all your office locations to make data-backed decisions on your back-to-office strategy.
- **Workplace and Workforce Metrics**: Stay informed of your workplace and workforce utilization with the help of graphs and metrics.

To learn more, see [Understanding Business Insights Architecture](https://help.zscaler.com/business-insights/understanding-business-insights-architecture).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/dspm-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2025-06-14T15:20Z","nid":"1483321"} -->
## DSPM Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/dspm-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > DSPM Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-14T15:20Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of data stores purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *data store* is a subscription for a single cloud service instance such as virtual machines (VMs), storage buckets, or databases that your organization utilizes in your public cloud environments.

The number of data stores required is determined by counting the total number of unique individual VMs (every instance is counted as one data store), storage buckets, databases, and any additional supported service that was configured as a scanned service by the customer over the subscription period.

An average volume cap for scanned data is considered as part of the fair use policy. If you exceed that average volume cap, additional volume add-on is required.

Ensure that you order the correct number of data stores. If additional data stores are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of data stores that the service monitors to ensure license compliance.

You should deploy DSPM for the number of licenses ordered using selective account onboarding. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of monitored data stores and can work with you to purchase additional licenses as needed, based on usage.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of DSPM is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy). The average volume of scanned data per data store is expected to be less than two times the observed average across Zscaler customers (currently 1TB per data store).

On average, across all subscribed data stores, the volume of scanned data should not exceed 1TB per data store. The volume of some data stores can exceed 1TB, provided that the average volume when calculated across all subscribed data stores remains below 1TB.

If the usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/dspm-logs","lastmod":"2025-07-28T08:04Z","nid":"1483311"} -->
## DSPM Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/dspm-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > DSPM Logs
- Last modified: 2025-07-28T08:04Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) logs.

Cloud configuration data, Cloud Service Provider (CSP) activity audit logs, and cloud user directory information are processed by Zscaler in connection with your organization's use of Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM).

In addition, subject to customer configuration and enablement, the following logs are also processed:

- Data residing in cloud data stores such as databases, storage services and data volumes (disks) is scanned and classified. Raw data is not saved, only static metadata is stored and reported.
- CSP-hosted virtual machines operating system drive is scanned for installed packages and vulnerabilities (CVEs).

All logs that describe active cloud resources or issues are retained by Zscaler for the duration of the subscription. Once the resources are no longer present in the CSP, DSPM maintains the logs for a rolling period of 180 days during the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes the logs after the 180-day retention cycle or earlier upon request. By accessing the DSPM service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/easm-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2025-06-18T05:55Z","nid":"1504046"} -->
## Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/easm-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-18T05:55Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed in various ways. This article includes information on licensing types, the license renewal process, and Zscaler’s Fair Use Policy.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following two types of licenses:

- Seat: A subscription license for the Zscaler EASM service for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required is determined by counting the total number of unique individual users of Zscaler EASM over the previous rolling 90-day period.
- Asset: A subscription license for the number of unique public internet-facing corporate assets discovered by EASM such as:
  - Domains
  - Hosts
  - Web pages
  - SSL/TLS certificates
  - IP addresses

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats or assets. If you require additional seats or assets, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of users and assets to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of EASM is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for EASM is that under the seat license type, the asset to seat ratio may not exceed 0.75. Usage exceeding the Fair Use Policy requires a subscription for additional entitlements. Contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/easm-logs","lastmod":"2025-12-03T11:36Z","nid":"1504036"} -->
## Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/easm-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM) Logs
- Last modified: 2025-12-03T11:36Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler External Attack Surface Management ( EASM) logs.

For Zscaler External Attack Surface Management (EASM), *logs* are defined as public internet-facing assets that are discovered and scanned by Zscaler EASM to identify and analyze potential external attack surfaces. These public internet-facing corporate assets include:

- Domains
- Hosts
- Web pages
- SSL/TLS certificates
- IP addresses

Zscaler retains log information for a rolling period of 14 days during the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler after the 14-day retention cycle or earlier upon request.

Logs are stored in the United States.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

- Summary: Information about Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to a number of seats purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *seat*is a subscription license for the ZDX service for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required is determined by counting the total number of unique individual users of ZDX over the previous rolling 90-day period.

## ZDX Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zdx-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > ZDX Logs
- Last modified: 2026-06-26T10:32Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX) logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX) service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

- **Definition:** For ZDX,*logs* are defined as the telemetry metadata collected via ZDX probes and Microsoft 365 probes, as well as the metadata that correlates with logs of other Zscaler SaaS products, such as Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) or Zscaler Private Access (ZPA).
- **Retention:** Zscaler retains the logs on a rolling period of at least two weeks or two days during your subscription term, depending on your subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
- **Storage Location:** Logs are stored in the United States, European Union, Australia, Canada, Singapore, or India. If you subscribe to the ZDX Data Residency feature, the logs are stored in the geographic region selected by you.

###### ZDX Diagnostics Mode

- **Description:** ZDX supports Diagnostics mode to enable remote live diagnostics and troubleshooting by an administrator.
- **Data Collected:** Diagnostics might result in the capture and storage of packet capture files, as well as additional telemetry about user devices, including software process level information of the devices (i.e., ZDX Deep Tracing data).
- **Retention:** Zscaler retains the ZDX Diagnostics reports on a rolling period of at least two weeks or two days during your subscription term, depending on your subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the ZDX Diagnostics reports and Diagnostics data are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

###### Feature-specific Information

- **ZDX Snapshot:** The ZDX Snapshot feature captures the current state of a UI page, and provides a URL that admins can share with ZDX users or other admins for view-only access. ZDX Snapshots are retained by Zscaler for 90 days.
- **ZDX Copilot:** ZDX Copilot prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 14 days as part of the session history. ZDX Copilot is not trained using any customer data.
- **ZDX Network Intelligence:** Aggregated logs are retained by Zscaler for a period of one year.
- **ZDX Managed Monitoring:** Logs are retained by Zscaler for a period of 30 days.
- **ZDX Remediation:** ZDX Remediation allows for the execution of remote scripts on user devices. Enabling this feature allows the collection of script output and device telemetry data. All script results and telemetry collected through this feature are retained by Zscaler for 180 days. Authorized users can delete script results at any time via the ZDX Admin Portal.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zero-trust-branch-connector-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2025-06-10T10:59Z","nid":"1468116"} -->
## Zero Trust Branch Connector Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zero-trust-branch-connector-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zero Trust Branch Connector Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-10T10:59Z
- Summary: Information about Zero Trust Branch Connector licensing and fair use.

Zero Trust Branch Connector is a Software as a Service (SaaS) that is licensed by the number of sites/locations being protected and the data usage of the protected devices/services for the subscription term. A device/server is defined as an endpoint such as a printer, camera, badge reader, RF scanners, IoT, IIoT, IoMT, server, virtual desktop instances, or other items that have a unique IP address, cannot be used with Zscaler Client Connector software, and are typically located in branch offices, campuses, and data center on-prem locations. If you have a Guest Wi-Fi subscription, all gigabyte (GB) usage and endpoints are excluded from the overall GB allowed from the site.

The number of protected devices is determined by counting the unique IP addresses for each of the protected endpoint types and applying the number to the subscription term. These unique IP addresses are counted at an hourly interval. The total count is calculated by averaging the hourly count over a month. All endpoints and data transfers (in GB) accounted for in Guest Wi-Fi SKUs are excluded.

Ensure that you order the correct number of sites and additional data usage as needed. If additional data usage is needed during a subscription term, refer to Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler monitors and periodically reviews the number of licensed protected workloads and their bandwidth usage to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of Zero Trust Branch Connector is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for Zero Trust Branch Connector is that the average data transfer from 50 devices/servers per site is 100 GB for each month. If the usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zero Trust Browser Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zero-trust-browser-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zero Trust Browser Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-04-01T09:26Z
- Summary: Information about Zero Trust Browser Licensing and Fair Use.

Zero Trust Browser (including Zero Trust Cloud Browser, Zero Trust Browser Extension, and Zero Trust Enterprise Browser) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of seats purchased for the subscription term in an order.

A *seat* is a subscription license for the Zero Trust Browser service for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required is determined by calculating the total number of unique individual users of the Zero Trust Browser service over a rolling 90-day period.

Your usage of the Zero Trust Cloud Browser service is also subject to the data consumption limits stated in your Zero Trust Browser SKU. If your purchased SKU does not state a specific data limit, your usage is subject to the parameters of the Fair Use Policy below.

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats. If you require additional seats during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of Zero Trust Browser is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/acceptable-use-policy). To maintain optimal performance and stability across the Zscaler multi-tenant cloud, data consumption is limited to the stated data limits in the purchased SKU. If no data limits are explicitly mentioned, then the allowable average monthly traffic across all purchased seats must be less than two times (2x) the current cloud-wide average (currently 8 GB per seat per month), plus any additional bandwidth entitlements explicitly stated in your contract. This Fair Use Policy encompasses all data uploaded and downloaded via the Zero Trust Cloud Browser.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zia-china-premium-and-premium-plus-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-07-06T14:12Z","nid":"1538481"} -->
## ZIA China Premium and Premium Plus Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zia-china-premium-and-premium-plus-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > ZIA China Premium and Premium Plus Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-06T14:12Z
- Summary: Information about ZIA China Premium and Premium Plus Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) China Premium and ZIA China Premium Plus are Software as a Service (SaaS) products that are licensed according to the bandwidth purchased for the subscription term in an order. To learn more, see [Managing ZIA Use in China](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/managing-zia-use-china).

## ZIA China Premium

For ZIA China Premium, *bandwidth* is defined as the amount of data that is transmitted over a network connection and processed by ZIA within a Premium data center operated by Zscaler in China. Bandwidth is calculated in Megabits per second (Mbps) using five-minute samples. Zscaler calculates bandwidth based on Received (Rx) and Transmitted (Tx) Mbps. All five-minute samples from a data center in a calendar month are sorted, and the 95th percentile value is taken (P95 Accounting Method). This calculation is done separately for both the Tx and Rx values. The larger of the two is used as that data center's bandwidth usage. The P95 Accounting Method is calculated for each Premium data center accessed each month. The P95 Accounting Method bandwidth usage values from all Premium data centers are combined (summed) in order to compute the total bandwidth usage for that calendar month.

You must remain within your purchased bandwidth for 95% of the time in any calendar month. By calculating monthly bandwidth usage at the 95th percentile, you can burst above your purchased bandwidth for up to 5% of the month without incurring additional charges. In a 30-day calendar month, this represents approximately 36 hours.

Ensure that you order the correct amount of bandwidth. If you require additional bandwidth, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. If you exceed your total purchased bandwidth, you shall promptly reduce your bandwidth usage until it is within the purchased bandwidth amount or place an order for additional bandwidth. Zscaler periodically reviews bandwidth usage to ensure license compliance.

In order to protect the ZIA China Premium quality of service, Zscaler reserves the right to deploy bandwidth control policies to restrict bandwidth consumption to within purchased bandwidth.

When calculating bandwidth consumption, in addition to internal tools, Zscaler may use reports from 3rd-party network and internet service providers. Upon written request, Zscaler will provide bandwidth usage reports for the previous calendar month.

Your use of ZIA China Premium is subject to the terms of Zscaler's [Supplemental Premium China Services Availability Agreement](https://www.zscaler.com/china-premium-access-productsheet). The Service Availability Agreement will not apply if you exceed the burst limits (greater than 130% at any time and/or greater than 5% of five-minute samples in a calendar month).

## Fair Use Policy

The maximum burst bandwidth may not exceed 130% of the purchased bandwidth at any time. Excess bursting bandwidth (whether excess in time or in bandwidth) is only available on a best-effort basis and may be subject to throttling down to your purchased bandwidth.

|  | Purchased Bandwidth (Mbps) | Peak bandwidth value (five-minute sample) | Burst duration (percentage of five-minute samples  above purchased bandwidth) | Within Limits? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Example 1 | 140 | 200 | 5% | No. Peak value exceeds 130% of purchased bandwidth |
| Example 2 | 140 | 180 | 5% | Yes |
| Example 3 | 140 | 170 | 6% | No. Burst duration exceeds 5%  of five-minute samples |

The usage of ZIA China Premium is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).

## ZIA China Premium Plus

For ZIA China Premium Plus, *bandwidth* is defined as the amount of data that is transmitted over a network connection and processed by ZIA within a Premium Plus data center operated by Zscaler in China. Bandwidth is calculated in Megabits per second (Mbps) using five-minute samples. Zscaler calculates bandwidth based on Received (Rx) and Transmitted (Tx) Mbps. All five-minute samples from a data center in a calendar month are sorted, and the highest value is taken (Peak Accounting Method). This calculation is done separately for both the Tx and Rx values. The larger of the two is used as that data center's bandwidth usage. The Peak Accounting Method is calculated for each Premium Plus data center accessed each month. The Peak Accounting Method bandwidth usage values from all Premium Plus data centers are combined (summed) in order to compute the total bandwidth usage for that calendar month. The bursting limitations applicable to ZIA China Premium do not apply to ZIA China Premium Plus.

Ensure that you order the correct amount of bandwidth. If you require additional bandwidth, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. If you exceed your total purchased bandwidth, you shall promptly reduce your bandwidth usage until it is within the purchased bandwidth amount or place an order for additional bandwidth. Zscaler periodically reviews bandwidth usage to ensure license compliance.

In order to protect the ZIA China Premium Plus quality of service, Zscaler reserves the right to deploy bandwidth control policies to restrict bandwidth consumption to within purchased bandwidth.

When calculating bandwidth consumption, in addition to internal tools, Zscaler may use reports from 3rd-party network and internet service providers. Upon written request, Zscaler will provide bandwidth usage reports for the previous calendar month.

Your use of ZIA China Premium Plus is subject to the terms of Zscaler's [Supplemental Premium China Services Availability Agreement](https://www.zscaler.com/china-premium-access-productsheet).

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of ZIA China Premium Plus is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zia-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-02-27T07:45Z","nid":"1390816"} -->
## ZIA Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zia-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > ZIA Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-02-27T07:45Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that can be licensed in various ways. This article includes information on licensing types, license renewal process, and Zscaler’s Fair Use Policy.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following types of licenses:

- Seat: A subscription license for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required for ZIA is determined by counting the total number of unique individual users of ZIA over the previous rolling 90-day period. The total endpoints across all seats may not exceed three times the number of seats purchased.
- Site: A subscription license for a site or location that enables Zero Trust SD-WAN and/or Internet of Things (IoT) device visibility. For an IoT site, only the parent location is counted. In the case of an IoT hub-and-spoke deployment, the spokes or branches behind the hub are each counted as a site. Each site includes a specific number of devices based on the site subscription type.
- ZIA Monthly Traffic: The total amount of Authenticated Traffic and Unauthenticated Traffic that is uploaded and downloaded via ZIA in a calendar month, measured in GB. For these purposes, *Authenticated Traffic* means traffic sent and received by a known seat. *Unauthenticated Traffic* means traffic not related to a known seat, including inline guest Wi-Fi, device, server, and workload traffic.
- Workload: For subscriptions licensed per workload (instead of per GB of Monthly Traffic), including but not limited to Zscaler Workload Communications, a *workload* is defined as a unique domain name, an IP address, or a set of IP addresses. A workload can be virtual machines (VMs), virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), serverless functions, and container-based resources deployed in customer public cloud and data center environments.
- Data Center: For subscriptions licensed per data center, such as Zscaler Managed Dedicated IP, a *data center* is defined as a Zscaler data center with which the pair of IP addresses subscribed to by you are associated. The same pair of IP addresses cannot be transferred to a different data center during the lifetime of the subscription.

Zero Trust Browser (Isolation or Cloud Browser Isolation) and Source IP Anchoring (SIPA) are subscribed per seat with a maximum aggregate amount of ZIA Monthly Traffic across all seats.

If you order ZIA China Premium or Premium Plus Services, please see the additional disclosures at [ZIA China Premium and Premium Plus Licensing and Fair Use](https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zia-china-premium-and-premium-plus-licensing-and-fair-use).

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats, sites, workloads, or amount of monthly traffic. If you require additional seats, sites, workloads, or monthly traffic, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats, sites, workloads, and amount of monthly traffic to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of ZIA is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for ZIA is the average ZIA Monthly Traffic across all seats purchased should be less than two times the cloud-wide average (currently 8 GB per seat per month) plus any additional bandwidth entitlement you have. Unauthenticated traffic in excess of this Fair Use Policy requires a subscription for additional bandwidth. Contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
