<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zia-logs","lastmod":"2026-08-05T11:50Z","nid":"1391021"} -->
## ZIA Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zia-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > ZIA Logs
- Last modified: 2026-08-05T11:50Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

- **Definition:** For ZIA, *logs* are defined as network traffic metadata for your SaaS applications.
- **Retention:** Zscaler retains the logs for a rolling period of six months during the term of subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logsare deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
- **Storage:** During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union and Switzerland.

###### Feature-specific Information

- **Data Loss Prevention (DLP):** The Data Loss Prevention (DLP) service (for any channel such as Inline, Endpoint, Email, API CASB, or Private Applications), logs also capture metadata for certain end user activities, such as copying to removable storage, copying to network shares, printing, sharing a file, and uploading a document. For the Email DLP service, logs include the senders, recipients, and subjects of emails.
- **Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS):** Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) allows you to stream the logs in real-time within your premises. Using NSS, these logs can also be sent to multiple systems, allowing the retention of the logs for any period.
- **Gen AI Security:** Gen AI Security logs will also include classifications of end user prompts to generative AI applications. By default, end user prompts to supported generative AI applications are not captured in logs. They are captured in the logs only if your administrator enables this feature via the toggle in the Admin Portal.
- **IoT Advanced Security:** For the IoT Advanced Security service, unauthenticated, non-user-identifying web logs that are associated with the customer at the org level will be retained by Zscaler for a rolling period of three months during the term of subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, these logs are deleted by Zscaler after the three month retention cycle. For the IoT Advanced Security service, the logs will be stored in the United States.
- **Endpoint Context:** Endpoint Context service logs also capture telemetry about user devices. This telemetry may include software process level information of the device.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## ZPA China Premium Service Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpa-china-premium-service-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > ZPA China Premium Service Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-06T14:13Z
- Summary: Information about ZPA China Premium Service Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) China Premium is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the bandwidth purchased for the subscription term in an order. To learn more, see [Managing ZPA Use in China](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/managing-zpa-use-china).

For ZPA China Premium, *bandwidth* is defined as the amount of data that is transmitted over a network connection and processed by ZPA within a Premium Data Center operated by Zscaler in China. Bandwidth is calculated in Megabits per second (Mbps) using five-minute samples. Zscaler calculates bandwidth based on Received (Rx) and Transmitted (Tx) Mbps. All five-minute samples from a data center in a calendar month are sorted, and the 95th percentile value is taken (P95 Accounting Method). This calculation is done separately for both the Tx and Rx values. The larger of the two is used as that data center's bandwidth usage. The P95 Accounting Method is calculated for each Premium Data Center accessed each month. The P95 Accounting Method bandwidth usage values from all Premium Data Centers are combined (summed) in order to compute the total bandwidth usage for that calendar month.

You must remain within your purchased bandwidth for 95% of the time in any calendar month. By calculating monthly bandwidth usage at the 95th percentile, you can burst above your purchased bandwidth for up to 5% of the month without incurring additional charges. In a 30-day calendar month, this represents approximately 36 hours.

Ensure that you order the correct amount of bandwidth. If you require additional bandwidth, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. If you exceed your total purchased bandwidth, you shall promptly reduce your bandwidth usage until it is within the purchased bandwidth amount or place an order for additional bandwidth. Zscaler periodically reviews bandwidth usage to ensure license compliance.

In order to protect the Zscaler ZPA China Premium quality of service, Zscaler reserves the right to deploy bandwidth control policies to restrict bandwidth consumption to within purchased bandwidth.

When calculating bandwidth consumption, in addition to internal tools, Zscaler may use reports from 3rd-party network and internet service providers. Upon written request, Zscaler will provide bandwidth usage reports for the previous calendar month.

Your use of ZPA China Premium is subject to the terms of Zscaler's [Supplemental Premium China Services Availability Agreement](https://www.zscaler.com/china-premium-access-productsheet). The Service Availablility Agreement will not apply if you exceed the burst limits (greater than 130% at any time and/or greater than 5% of five-minute samples in a calendar month).

## Fair Use Policy

The maximum burst bandwidth may not exceed 130% of the purchased bandwidth at any time. Excess bursting bandwidth (whether excess in time or in bandwidth) is only available on a best-effort basis and may be subject to throttling down to your purchased bandwidth.

|  | Purchased Bandwidth (Mbps) | Peak bandwidth value (five-minute sample) | Burst duration (percentage of five-minute samples  above purchased bandwidth) | Within Limits? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Example 1 | 140 | 200 | 5% | No, peak value exceeds 130% of purchased bandwidth |
| Example 2 | 140 | 180 | 5% | Yes |
| Example 3 | 140 | 170 | 6% | No, burst duration exceeds 5% of five-minute samples |

The usage of ZPA China Premium is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zpa-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-03-09T08:37Z","nid":"1390801"} -->
## ZPA Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpa-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > ZPA Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-03-09T08:37Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed in various ways. This article includes information on licensing types, the license renewal process, and Zscaler’s Fair Use Policy.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following types of licenses:

- Seat: A subscription license for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required is determined by counting the total number of unique individual users of ZPA over the previous rolling 90-day period.
- Site: A subscription license for a site or location that enables Zero Trust SD-WAN. Each site includes a specific number of devices based on the site subscription type.
- ZPA Monthly Traffic: The total amount of traffic that is uploaded and downloaded via ZPA in a calendar month, measured in GB.
- System: Each system is equivalent to an RDP, SSH, VNC or RealVNC target that enables Privileged Remote Access (PRA).
- Workload: For subscriptions licensed per workload (instead of per GB of monthly traffic), including but not limited to Zscaler Workload Communications, a *workload* is defined as a unique domain name, an IP address, or a set of IP addresses. A workload can be virtual machines (VMs), virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), serverless functions, and container-based resources deployed in your public cloud and data center environments.

Browser Isolation (i.e., Zero Trust Browser, formerly Isolation) and Source IP Anchoring (SIPA) are subscribed per seat with a maximum aggregate amount of ZPA Monthly Traffic across all seats. ZPA B2B Federation is subscribed per seat.

If you order ZPA China Premium Service, please see the additional disclosures at [ZPA China Premium Service Licensing and Fair Use](https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpa-china-premium-service-licensing-and-fair-use).

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats, sites, workloads, or amount of monthly traffic. If you require additional seats, sites, workloads, or monthly traffic, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats, sites, workloads, and amount of monthly traffic to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of ZPA is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for ZPA is the average monthly traffic across all seats purchased should be less than two times the cloud-wide average (currently 3 GB per seat per month) plus any additional bandwidth entitlement you have. Use of ZPA monthly traffic in excess of this Fair Use Policy requires a subscription for additional entitlements. Contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zpa-logs","lastmod":"2025-11-24T11:42Z","nid":"1390951"} -->
## ZPA Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpa-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > ZPA Logs
- Last modified: 2025-11-24T11:42Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) logs.

In order to access the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For ZPA, *logs* are defined as follows:

- User Logs: Activity logs of authorized users who access your internal applications through ZPA. These logs capture end-user requests to Applications or information related to an end user's availability and connection to ZPA. To learn more, see [User Activity Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/user-activity-log-fields) and [User Status Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/user-status-log-fields).
- App Connector Logs: Activity logs of the App Connector, which allow authorized users access to your internal applications through ZPA. These logs capture information on an App Connector's availability and connection to ZPA. To learn more, see [App Connector Status Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/connector-status-log-fields).
- AppProtection Logs: Activity logs relating to the inspection of traffic destined to or from internal applications through ZPA.
- API Discovery Logs: Activity logs (derived from AppProtection Logs) that capture information about discovered APIs within your environment and associated users of those APIs.
- Audit Logs: Activity logs of configuration changes you made via the ZPA Admin Portal. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-audit-logs) and [Audit Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-audit-log-fields).
- Privileged Session Recordings: Screen recordings of RDP, SSH, VNC systems by users accessed in Privileged Remote Access (PRA) configured with the Record Session Privileged Capability. To learn more, see [About Consoles Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-consoles-policy) and Viewing Recordings in [Accessing Privileged Sessions](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-sessions).
- Privileged Session Files: Files uploaded by users within PRA configured with a Portal Policy. To learn more, see [About Portals Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-portals-policy).
- Zscaler Microsegmentation Agent Logs: Agent logs that include information such as hostname, operating system name, operating system version, network addresses, cloud environment details (i.e., Cloud Name, Cloud Account ID, Cloud Region, VPC/VNET details, Cloud Subnet details, user defined tags in cloud), traffic connection information and host resource telemetry (i.e., CPU, memory, file descriptor utilization).

Logs do not include your internal system logs.

Zscaler retains User Activity, User Status, Inspection, and App Connector log information for a rolling period of at least 14 days during the subscription term. Zscaler retains audit log information for a rolling period of six months during the subscription term. If you subscribe to the Extended Retention feature, Zscaler retains User Activity, User Status, Inspection, and App Connector log information for a rolling period of six months during the subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention cycles. You can also view your logs or stream logs in real-time using the [Log Streaming Service (LSS)](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-log-streaming-service).

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.

If you order the VPN Connectivity service, logs also include:

- VPN Connector Logs: Activity logs of the VPN Connector, which allow authorized users access to your internal applications through ZPA VPN Connectivity. These logs capture information on a VPN Connector’s availability and connection to ZPA.
- VPN Service Edge Logs: Activity logs of the VPN Service Edge which enables secure VPN tunnels from the user and from the VPN Connector and routes data from authorized users to internal destination applications.

If you configure the Session Recording for PRA, session recordings will be retained by Zscaler for a period of one year during the term of subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, these logs are deleted by Zscaler. For the PRA Session Recording service, the session recordings will be encrypted and stored in the geographical region in which your tenant is located.

If you subscribe to Zscaler Microsegmentation machine-learning recommendations (and opt-in to receive these recommendations), Zscaler will store flow logs and resource inventory data for a rolling period of up to 180 days. This data will be used for generating recommendations. To learn more about flow logs, see [About Flow Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-flow-logs). To learn more about resource inventory data, see [About Resources](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-resources).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## ZPC Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpc-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > ZPC Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-10T11:55Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of workloads purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *workload* is a subscription for a single cloud workload such as virtual machines (VMs), serverless functions, and container resources that your organization utilizes in your public cloud environments.

The number of workloads required is determined by counting the unique individual VMs (every VM is counted as one workload), serverless functions (every 5 serverless functions count as one workload), and containers (every 5 containers count as one workload) over the subscription period.

Ensure that you order the correct number of workloads. If additional workloads are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of workloads that the service monitors to ensure license compliance.

You should deploy ZPC for the number of licenses ordered using selective account onboarding. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of monitored workloads and can work with you to purchase additional licenses as needed, based on usage.

The usage of ZPC is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zpc-logs","lastmod":"2025-02-10T18:53Z","nid":"1403221"} -->
## ZPC Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zpc-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > ZPC Logs
- Last modified: 2025-02-10T18:53Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) logs.

Cloud configuration data, Cloud Service Provider (CSP) activity audit logs, cloud network logs, and cloud user directory information are processed by Zscaler in connection with your organization's use of Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC).

Depending on the acquired subscription and permissions granted by the customer, the following logs are also processed:

- For customers opting for the vulnerability scanning subscription (ZPC Vulnerability or ZPC Advanced), Zscaler further analyzes the content of CSP-hosted virtual machines operating system drive and container images. (subject to customer configuration and enablement)
- For customers opting for the Infrastructure as Code (ZPC IaC or ZPC Advanced) subscription, Zscaler further analyzes the content of IaC scripts in the user code repositories or CI/CD tools. (subject to customer configuration and enablement)

All logs that describe active cloud resources or issues are retained by Zscaler for the duration of the subscription. Once the resources are no longer present in the CSP, ZPC maintains the logs for a rolling period of 180 days during the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes the logs after the 180-day retention cycle. By accessing the ZPC service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler Adaptive Access Engine Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-adaptive-access-engine-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Adaptive Access Engine Logs
- Last modified: 2025-09-03T14:02Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Adaptive Access Engine logs and data retention.

By accessing the Zscaler Adaptive Access Engine service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Adaptive Access Engine, *logs* are defined as follows:

- Signal History: Security context signals received from Zscaler products such as Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and third-party security products that typically indicate a level of risk for a user or device.
- Audit Logs: Activity records of configuration changes made in the Admin Portal and via the Adaptive Access Engine API.

Zscaler retains the Signal History for a rolling period of 90 days during the term of the subscription. Zscaler retains Audit Log information for a rolling period of 6 months during the subscription term.

When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention cycles.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler Agentic SecOps Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-agentic-secops-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Agentic SecOps Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T10:01Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Agentic SecOps Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Agentic SecOps is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of seats purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *seat* is a subscription license for the Agentic SecOps product for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required for a subscription of Agentic SecOps is determined by the total number of unique individual users of the underlying SaaS product to be analyzed by Agentic SecOps over the previous rolling 90-day period.

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats. If you require additional seats during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of Agentic SecOps is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for Agentic SecOps is that the average data processing (uncompressed) is expected to be no more than 10MB per user on a daily basis. If the usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler Agentic SecOps Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-agentic-secops-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Agentic SecOps Logs
- Last modified: 2026-06-26T09:43Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Agentic SecOps Logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Agentic SecOps service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

- **Definition:** For Agentic SecOps, *logs* are defined as the configuration and transaction data collected for actions performed by users authorized by you who are using the Agentic SecOps SaaS product. This includes duplicates of applicable Zscaler SaaS product logs, such as Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) or Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), that Zscaler uses to identify suspicious and potentially malicious threat patterns for you.
- **Retention:** Depending on your subscription, Zscaler retains Agentic SecOps logs for a rolling period of up to six months during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
- **Storage Location:** During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.

###### Feature-specific information

- **Incident:** For incidents identified by Agentic SecOps, the information related to such incidents is stored by Zscaler for one year.
- **Comments:** For the Comments feature, your comments are stored by Zscaler for up to one year, as long as the related incident remains on the platform.
- **Mapping Copilot:** For the Mapping Copilot feature, prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 90 days as part of the session history. Mapping Copilot is not trained using any customer data.
- **ASOC Assist:** ASOC Assist is the AI-powered assistant in Agentic SecOps. For the ASOC Assist feature, prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 90 days as part of the session history. ASOC Assist is not trained using any customer data.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-ai-asset-management-ai-infrastructure-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T13:05Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of AI assets purchased for the subscription term in an order. An *AI asset* is a subscription license for the AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure service for an individual authorized custom AI application, AI model, Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint, or AI agent that you use in your public cloud environments (e.g. AWS Bedrock) or SaaS AI builder platform (e.g. Microsoft Copilot Studio).

The number of AI assets required is the total number of unique individual custom AI applications, AI models, MCP endpoints, AI agents, and any additional supported service that is configured as a scanned service by you during the subscription period. You should deploy AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure for the number of AI assets ordered using selective account onboarding.

Ensure that you order the correct number of AI assets. If additional AI assets are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of data stores that the service monitors to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure is the average volume of scanned data per data store/platform is expected to be less than two times the cloud-wide average. Currently, 1TB per data store/platform per month. This means that the volume of some data stores/platforms can exceed 1TB, provided that the average volume across all data stores/platforms remains below 1TB. The amount of data scanned is based on your scan settings. The volume of scanned data in excess of this Fair Use Policy requires a subscription for additional volume. Contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

In order to provide the Zscaler AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

- **Definition:** For AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure service, *logs* are defined as cloud configuration data, Cloud Service Provider (CSP) activity audit logs, and cloud user directory information. In addition, subject to your configuration and enablement, the following logs are also processed:
  - Static metadata of data residing in cloud data stores such as databases, storage services and data volumes (i.e., disks).
  - CSP-hosted virtual machine's operating system drive is scanned for installed packages and vulnerabilities (i.e., CVEs).
- **Retention:** All logs that describe active cloud resources or issues are retained by Zscaler for the duration of the subscription. Once the resources are no longer present in the CSP, AI Asset Management for AI Infrastructure retains the logs for a rolling period of 180 days during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles or earlier upon request.
- **Storage Location:** Logs are stored in the United States.

## Zscaler AI Asset Management Platform Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-ai-asset-management-platform-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler AI Asset Management Platform Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T13:07Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler AI Asset Management Platform Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler AI Asset Management Platform is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to a number of seats purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *seat* is a subscription license for the AI Asset Management Platform service for an individual authorized user whose traffic is monitored for AI application usage. Licensing applies to visibility for:

- Generative AI applications
- Embedded AI applications
- Endpoint AI applications

A Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) tenant may be provisioned to capture your end-user traffic destined to AI applications. This ZIA tenant is provided only for AI Asset Management traffic visibility. You are not entitled to other ZIA capabilities (e.g., general internet traffic monitoring, web filtering, non-AI application traffic inspection, etc.) unless separately licensed under ZIA.

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats. If additional seats are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats that use the service to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of AI Asset Management Platform is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy). AI Asset Management Platform is intended for normal enterprise user traffic associated with AI application usage.

- Usage must be consistent with the number of purchased seats.
- Traffic must represent your end-user activity to generative AI (Gen AI), Embedded AI, and Endpoint AI apps.
- The service must not be used for automated, synthetic, or non-user-generated traffic at scale.
- You must not use the provisioned ZIA tenant for capabilities outside AI Asset Management.
- Zscaler may review usage to ensure alignment with the purchased subscription and intended product scope.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler AI Guard Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-ai-guard-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler AI Guard Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-01-27T09:44Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler AI Guard Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler AI Guard is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed based on a platform subscription fee and the number of tokens purchased for the subscription term in an order.

AI Guard uses transformers that tokenize prompts and responses. A *token* is the standard non-divisible metric of consumption used by Generative AI models. A token is generally considered to be four characters, using UTF-8 code points, excluding white space. AI Guard uses the total number of tokens in prompts and responses to calculate license consumption.

Ensure that you order the correct number of tokens for your application requirement. If you require additional tokens, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of tokens consumed to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zscaler AI Guard is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler AI Guard Logs
- Last modified: 2026-01-27T09:43Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler AI Guard Logs policy.

By using the Zscaler AI Guard Service, you grant Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify and display information from logs.

For AI Guard, *logs* are defined as the data collected in the form of prompts, responses, and other metadata.

Zscaler collects and stores metadata such as application name, policy triggered, and timestamp. If you opt in to the Store Prompt/Responses feature, the service will store end user prompts and prompt responses. If AI Guard is deployed as a proxy, LLM details will also be stored.

You have the option to encrypt the prompts and prompt responses using your organization’s encryption key.

Logs are stored for a period of 90 days. When your subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention cycles.

## Zscaler AI Scanning Platform Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-ai-scanning-platform-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler AI Scanning Platform Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-01-14T11:24Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler AI Scanning Platform Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler AI Scanning Platform is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed based on a platform subscription fee and the number of Probe Units purchased for the subscription term in an order.

## License Types

A *Probe Unit* is the standard non-divisible metric of consumption on the AI Scanning Platform. Probe Units come in the following two types:

- Standard Probe: A single discrete analysis function executed by the AI Scanning Platform on an AI system.
- Large Probe: A single discrete analysis function executed by the AI Scanning Platform which exceeds 200 test cases. The number of test cases is based on configurations defined in custom datasets, custom probes, RAG Precision scans, or Q&A scans.

A *Scanner Run* is a bundled simultaneous execution on an AI system of multiple distinct Standard Probes or Large Probes. Probe Units are consumed when you execute a Standard Probe, Large Probe, or a Scanner Run. You decide which Probes or Scanners to run and at what frequency via the Admin Portal.

Ensure that you order the correct number of Probe Units for your AI system, model, or application requirements. If you require additional Probe Units, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of Probe Units consumed to ensure license compliance.

The usage of AI Scanning Platform is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy.](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy)
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

During the term of your subscription, you may delete specific data sets (i.e., CSV files you uploaded to the platform) directly from the Admin Portal. For data that cannot be removed via the Admin Portal, you may submit a request for manual deletion by our team. When your subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.

## Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-asset-exposure-management-aem-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-10T11:49Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Asset Exposure Management (AEM) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of assets purchased for the subscription term in an order. The number of assets is counted as the number of assets processed and stored into AEM.

Ensure that you order the correct number of assets. If you require additional assets, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats, sites, workloads, and amount of monthly traffic to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of AEM is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for AEM is:

- The average data processing (uncompressed) is expected to be no more than 3MB per asset on a daily basis.
- The average number of daily queries per account is expected to be no more than 4K queries per day.

If the usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

For AEM, *logs* are defined as the configuration and transaction data collected for actions performed by users authorized by you who are acting within the AEM SaaS Application.

Zscaler retains the logs on a rolling period up to a year during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

For the Mapping Copilot feature, prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 90 days as part of the session history. Mapping Copilot is not trained using any customer data.

Logs are stored in the United States.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-cellular-sim-and-cellular-edge-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-03-31T08:58Z","nid":"1507401"} -->
## Zscaler Cellular (SIM and Cellular Edge) Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-cellular-sim-and-cellular-edge-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Cellular (SIM and Cellular Edge) Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-03-31T08:58Z
- Summary: Licensing and Fair Use information for Zscaler Cellular product.

Zscaler Cellular is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of cellular devices being protected and the data usage of the protected cellular devices for the subscription term in an order.

A *cellular device* is an endpoint with a Zscaler SIM (or e-SIM). The number of protected cellular devices is determined by the number of Zscaler SIMs purchased from Zscaler (for Zscaler SIM) or unique IP addresses accessing Zscaler Cellular Edge (for Cellular Edge).

A *data pool* is purchased for the protected cellular devices. This data pool can be used by any SIM/IP address assigned to that data pool. The data pool resets on the first day of each calendar month, and unused data is not carried over. For subscriptions beginning after the first day of a calendar month, the data pool and billing for the initial partial month will be prorated based on the number of remaining days in that month.

Ensure that you order the correct number of SIMs, IP addresses, and data usage as needed. If additional SIMs, IP addresses, or data usage are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler monitors and periodically reviews the number of protected cellular devices and their bandwidth usage to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zscaler Cellular is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy). If data usage exceeds the data pool limit within a calendar month, the service will continue without interruption and an overage charge will be incurred automatically at the pre-agreed rate per GB as specified in the applicable Order Form (such overage charges will co-term with the remainder of the Subscription Term). Overage charges are uncapped unless otherwise expressly stated in the applicable Order Form.

You acknowledge and agree that:

1. You are solely responsible for monitoring and managing your data usage.
2. Zscaler does not provide real-time usage alerts, spending caps, throttling or automatic service suspension.
3. Any usage dashboards or visibility tools Zscaler may provide are for informational purposes only and do not limit your payment obligations, including any overage charges.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-cellular-sim-and-cellular-edge-logs","lastmod":"2025-02-10T19:15Z","nid":"1507366"} -->
## Zscaler Cellular (SIM and Cellular Edge) Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-cellular-sim-and-cellular-edge-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Cellular (SIM and Cellular Edge) Logs
- Last modified: 2025-02-10T19:15Z
- Summary: Info about Zscaler Cellular (SIM and Cellular Edge) Logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler SIM and Zscaler Cellular Edge services, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

## Zscaler Cellular Edge Logs

Zscaler Cellular Edge logs are defined as Session Logs, Tunnel Logs, DNS Logs, and Audit Logs. To learn more, see [About Insights Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/about-insights-logs).

- Session Logs: Traffic flow of information related to the sessions originating from your cloud workloads. To learn more, see [Session Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/session-insights-logs-filters) and [Session Insights Log: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/session-insights-logs-columns).
- Tunnel Logs: Information related to the connectivity from the Cellular Edge to the Zscaler cloud. To learn more, see [Tunnel Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/zia-tunnel-insights-logs-filters) and [Tunnel Insights Logs: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/tunnel-insights-logs-columns).
- DNS Logs: Information related to the destination domains and the DNS responses for those domains. To learn more, see [DNS Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/dns-insights-logs-filters) and [DNS Insights Logs: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/dns-insights-logs-columns).
- Audit Logs: Zscaler Cellular Edge leverages the Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal, thus Audit Logs for Zscaler Cellular Edge consist of Activity logs of the configuration changes made via the Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal or API for Cloud Connector or Branch Connector. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/about-audit-logs).

## Zscaler SIM Logs

Logs for Zscaler SIM services will source information from the mobile network operators used, and include IMSI, IMEI, and CDR information.

These are only applicable to the Zscaler SIM services.

- SIM Event Logs: Whenever a device connects to the Zscaler Cellular Edge, the logging service will receive events like SIM authenticated time, location of the SIM card, network change, etc.
- SIM Data Usage Logs: Usage metrics like bytes transferred and time of usage from the mobile network operator.

## Retention Period

Zscaler retains log information for a rolling period of up to 180 days during the subscription term. Zscaler retains audit log information for a rolling period of six months during the subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention cycles. You can also view your logs or stream logs in real-time using the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-client-connector-logs","lastmod":"2025-12-15T16:31Z","nid":"1391061"} -->
## Zscaler Client Connector Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-client-connector-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Client Connector Logs
- Last modified: 2025-12-15T16:31Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Client Connector logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Client Connector service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

For Zscaler Client Connector, *logs* are defined as Packet Capture Logs, Client Connector Logs, and Tunnel Logs.

- Packet Capture Logs: Packet capture logs of your transactions. You can globally enable or disable the packet capture. You have unlimited access to these logs and can delete them from a laptop, desktop, or personal mobile device.
- Client Connector Logs: Client Connector logs capture information about the Zscaler Client Connector application and its usage on a given device. Log verbosity is configurable. Log information includes user interactions with the UI, for example, enabling and disabling services.
- Tunnel Logs: Logs the status, operation, and errors related to tunneling. These logs include information about which data centers the client is connecting to, profile and policy downloads, and requests for specific domains or websites.

To enhance support for you and improve system performance analysis, logs might also contain local performance and diagnostic metrics, including technical and operational metrics related to agents, devices, and authentication (referred to as *Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry*). If your log tenant is located in the European Union, you can enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry from the settings page within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal. Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry is enabled by default for all others with the option to opt-out within the same settings page described earlier. To learn more, see [Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles.](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/configuring-zscaler-client-connector-app-profiles)

Your logs are stored in the same location as your Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) logs (in the United States, European Union, or Australia).

Zscaler retains log information for a rolling period of at least 90 days during the subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

- Tunnel Logs: Information related to the connectivity from the Cloud Connector or Branch Connector to the Zscaler cloud. Your logs for Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector are retained by Zscaler for a rolling six month period during your subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler after the six month retention cycle.

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-deception-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Deception Logs
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T09:50Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Deception Logs.

By accessing Zscaler Deception, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Deception, *logs* are defined as follows:

- Security Telemetry Logs: The security telemetry data that is generated based on the interactions between the suspected attackers and the auto-generated decoys.
- Audit logs: The activity logs of configuration changes made by you on the Deception Admin Portal.

Logs do not include your internal system logs. Logs are retained by Zscaler for a rolling period of 12 months during the term of subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes the logs within 30 days. If you ordered the Deception log streaming service, then you can stream the logs in real-time to an on-premises solution. The logs can be sent to multiple systems that allow you to retain them for however long you choose.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have your logs stored in the United States, European Union, or Asia Pacific region. If you use GenAI Decoys ([Built with Llama](https://www.llama.com/llama3_1/license/)), inputs from potential threat actors will be processed in the US region for all customers.

- Last modified: 2026-07-30T13:11Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Experience Center Logs.

By accessing Zscaler Experience Center, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Experience Center, *logs* are defined as follows:

- **Definition:** Records of administrative access and usage within Experience Center.
- **Retention:** Zscaler retains Logs information for a rolling period of 14 days. When the term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention period.
- **Storage:** Logs are stored in the European Union for EU customers or in the United States for other customers.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-identity-protection-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-06-26T09:48Z","nid":"1541073"} -->
## Zscaler Identity Protection Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-identity-protection-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Identity Protection Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-06-26T09:48Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Identity Protection Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Identity Protection is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of user identities purchased for the subscription term in an order. The number of user identities is counted as the total number of user identities processed and stored in Identity Protection.

For Identity Protection, *user identity* means each unique individual whose identity is provisioned, managed, or otherwise represented within the Identity Protection SaaS application, regardless of whether such individual directly accesses or logs into the Identity Protection SaaS application.

Ensure that you order the correct number of user identities. If you require additional user identities, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of user identities to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of Identity Protection is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for Identity Protection is:

- The average data processing (uncompressed) is expected to be no more than 3MB per user identity on a daily basis.
- The average number of daily queries per account is expected to be no more than 4K queries per day.

If your usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-identity-protection-logs","lastmod":"2026-06-26T09:49Z","nid":"1541072"} -->
## Zscaler Identity Protection Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-identity-protection-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Identity Protection Logs
- Last modified: 2026-06-26T09:49Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Identity Protection Logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Identity Protection service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article. For Identity Protection, *logs* are defined as the configuration and transaction data collected for actions performed by users authorized by you who are acting within the Identity Protection SaaS application.

When Identity Protection is enabled, data is queried from your identity provider. The data and processed analytics are stored on the Security Operations Platform. This data is retained in the SecOps Platform for a rolling period of 12 months during the term of subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, Zscaler deletes this data within 30 days.

Zscaler retains the logs on a rolling period of up to 180 days during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

Logs are stored in the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-network-observability-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2025-06-10T12:43Z","nid":"1528601"} -->
## Zscaler Network Observability Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-network-observability-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Network Observability Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-10T12:43Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Network Observability Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Network Observability is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that can be licensed in various ways. This article includes information on licensing types, the license renewal process, and Zscaler’s Fair Use Policy.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following two types of licenses:

- Device: A subscription license for a monitored device. The number of devices is determined by counting the total number of unique IP addresses configured for Network Observability over the subscription period.
- Metrics: A subscription for the number of monitored metrics. The number of metrics that can be collected from each device is determined by the type of networking device. The full list for each device type is described in the documentation.

Ensure that you order the correct number of devices or metrics to be monitored. If additional devices or metrics to be monitored are needed during a subscription term, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of devices and metrics to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zscaler Network Observability is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

- Last modified: 2025-04-30T08:09Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Network Observability Logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Network Observability service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article. For Zscaler Network Observability, *logs* are defined as the network telemetry collected from Network Observability probes and your network devices. Zscaler retains the logs for a rolling period of ninety days during the subscription agreement. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Zscaler SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-saas-security-posture-management-sspm-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T11:49Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed according to the number of seats purchased for the subscription term in an order. A *seat* is a subscription to the SSPM SaaS for an individual authorized user. The number of seats required is determined by counting the total number of unique users accessing and/or using the SaaS over the previous rolling 90-day period.

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats. If you require additional seats, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of seats to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of SSPM is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/product-usage-terms/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for SSPM is that the average data transfer per subscribed seat should be less than two times the cloud-wide average (currently 8 GB per seat per month). Usage exceeding the Fair Use Policy requires a subscription for additional entitlements. Contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

## Zscaler SDK For Mobile Apps Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-sdk-mobile-apps-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler SDK For Mobile Apps Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-06-10T12:45Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler SDK for Mobile Apps Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler SDK for Mobile Apps (ZSDK) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed based on the number of Monthly Active Users (MAUs) for a given client mobile app for the subscription term in an order.

An *active user* is defined as an individual authorized user that logs into the client mobile app at least once during a calendar month. The number of MAUs required is determined by counting the total number of unique monthly active users over the previous rolling 90-day period.

Ensure that you order the correct number of MAUs. If you require additional MAUs, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the number of MAUs to ensure license compliance.

## Fair Use Policy

The usage of ZSDK is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/acceptable-use-policy). The Fair Use Policy for ZSDK is that the average monthly traffic per client mobile app is expected to be less than 950 TB. If the usage exceeds the acceptable amount, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner to discuss available options.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-sdk-mobile-apps-logs","lastmod":"2025-05-29T10:47Z","nid":"1529549"} -->
## Zscaler SDK For Mobile Apps Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-sdk-mobile-apps-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler SDK For Mobile Apps Logs
- Last modified: 2025-05-29T10:47Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler SDK for Mobile Apps Logs.

In order to access the Zscaler SDK for Mobile Apps (ZSDK) service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For ZSDK, *logs* are defined as follows:

- User Logs: Activity logs of authorized users who access your mobile application through ZSDK. These logs capture end user requests to applications, endpoint device metadata, or information related to an end user's availability and connection to Zscaler. To learn more, see [User Activity Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/user-activity-log-fields) and [User Status Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/user-status-log-fields).
- App Connector Logs: Activity logs of the App Connector. App Connectors allow authorized users access to your mobile application through ZSDK. These logs capture information on an App Connector's availability and connection to Zscaler. To learn more, see [App Connector Status Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/connector-status-log-fields).
- Audit Logs: Activity logs of configuration changes you made via the ZSDK Admin Portal. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-audit-logs) and [Audit Log Fields](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-audit-log-fields).

Logs do not include your internal system logs.

Zscaler retains User Logs and App Connector Logs for a rolling period of at least 14 days during the subscription term. Zscaler retains Audit Logs for a rolling period of six months during the subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to the applicable retention cycles. You can also view your logs or stream logs in real-time using the [Log Streaming Service (LSS)](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-log-streaming-service).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

## Zscaler Traffic Capture Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-traffic-capture-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Traffic Capture Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-07-21T11:15Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Traffic Capture licensing and fair use.

Zscaler Traffic Capture is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed by the number of seats and amount of data captured. The number of seats purchased for the subscription term is stated in an order. A *seat* is a subscription license for the Traffic Capture service for an individual authorized user. The amount of data captured is measured in aggregate on a monthly basis based on the number of seats and allocated amount of data captured per seat. The number of seats required is determined by counting the total number of unique individual users of Zscaler Traffic Capture over the previous rolling 90-day period.

Ensure that you order the correct number of seats and additional data usage as needed. If additional seats or data usage is needed during a subscription term, refer to Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler monitors and periodically reviews the number of seats and their data usage to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zscaler Traffic Capture is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-traffic-capture-logs","lastmod":"2026-07-21T11:13Z","nid":"1463506"} -->
## Zscaler Traffic Capture Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-traffic-capture-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Traffic Capture Logs
- Last modified: 2026-07-21T11:13Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Traffic Capture logs.

By accessing the Zscaler Traffic Capture service, you provide Zscaler the right to create PCAP files based on traffic and optionally decrypted content processed by Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA).

PCAP files can be created in multiple ways:

- Event-based capture: Available for supported actions in ZIA policies when a violation is matched.
- Capture-control: Available for Internet Access traffic based on your specific criteria.

A PCAP file contains captured network packet data, including headers and payload, associated with a specific policy criteria match, up to and including the specific connection depth that is created from a matching policy. You can limit the amount of data captured per matched policy and limit the frequency of capture (e.g., sampling 1 out of 10 or 100 transactions).

PCAP files are delivered directly to an external storage location provided by you. In order to ensure continuous delivery of the PCAP files, Zscaler retains the files in Streaming SIMD Extensions (SSE) memory for a limited period of time. Zscaler does not write PCAP files to disk.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

## Zscaler Zero Trust Branch Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-branch-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Zero Trust Branch Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-04-30T13:17Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Branch Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Zero Trust Branch is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed by the number of appliances enabled for protected devices during the subscription term.

A *device* is defined as an endpoint such as a printer, camera, badge reader, RF scanner, IoT, IIoT, IoMT, server, desktop instance, or other items that have a unique IP address.

The number of appliances enabled for segmentation is determined by counting the number of installed appliances for each of the protected devices and applying the number to the subscription term.

Ensure that you order the correct number of appliances. If additional appliances are needed during a subscription term, refer to Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler monitors and periodically reviews the number of appliances to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zero Trust Branch is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).

By accessing the Zscaler Zero Trust Branch service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Zero Trust Branch, *logs* are defined as Session Logs and Audit Logs.

- Session Logs: Traffic flow of information related to the sessions originating from endpoints connected to the Zscaler segmentation network.
- Audit Logs: Activity logs of the configuration changes made in the Zero Trust Branch Admin Portal or API.

Zscaler retains Session Logs for a rolling period of seven days during your subscription term. Zscaler retains Audit Logs for a rolling period of six months during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-browser-logs","lastmod":"2026-07-08T13:34Z","nid":"1539031"} -->
## Zscaler Zero Trust Browser Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-browser-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Zero Trust Browser Logs
- Last modified: 2026-07-08T13:34Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Browser Logs.

In order to provide the Zscaler Zero Trust Browser service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.

For Zero Trust Browser, *logs* are defined as follows:

- Agent Logs: Agent logs capture information related to the agent’s operational health and posture collection activities. The default logging level is set to Info.
- Workspaces Logs: Logs the status, operation, and errors related to user workspace management. These logs include information about whether the extension was installed using admin privilege, or which browser profile was created as per the installation/setup actions or failure/success related to the email validation for use of the product. The default log level is set to Info. The log verbosity is configurable by the user.
- Zero Trust Extension Tenant Dashboard Logs: These logs capture telemetry-related logs such as policy evaluation related to browsing activities, heartbeat, authentication, audit, and diagnostic logs. They also capture configuration change logs such as policy modifications and administrative audit logs.

For the Cloud Browser Isolation feature, logs may also capture passwords that are entered by the user for password-protected files. This is required to allow viewing the file from within the Zero Trust Browser.

To enhance support and improve system performance analysis, logs may also contain local performance and diagnostic metrics, including technical and operational metrics related to network calls or time taken to perform actions like posture collections.

The Agent Logs and Workspaces Logs are stored on your users’ local machines and are only accessible by your users and administrators. These logs are not stored in Zscaler clouds. In case of any specific failure that you want to report to Zscaler, Zscaler will process, store, and use these logs for debugging purposes.

Zero Trust Extension Tenant Dashboard Logs are retained by Zscaler for the term of the subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler after one month.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the Zero Trust Extension Tenant Dashboard Logs stored in the United States, the European Union, Singapore, or India.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-device-segmentation-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2026-01-08T10:32Z","nid":"1514416"} -->
## Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-device-segmentation-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2026-01-08T10:32Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation (formerly Airgap) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed by the number of gateways enabled for protected devices during the subscription term.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following two types of licenses:

- Device: A subscription license for an endpoint such as a printer, camera, badge reader, RF scanner, IoT, IIoT, IoMT, server, desktop instance, or other items that have a unique IP address.
- Gateway: A subscription license for a piece of hardware or virtual machine sitting between different networks or applications

The number of gateways enabled for segmentation is determined by counting the number of installed gateways for each of the protected devices and applying the number to the subscription term. You may purchase additional entitlements allowing the addition of additional devices to a gateway.

Ensure that you order the correct number of gateways and devices. If additional gateways or devices are needed during a subscription term, refer to Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler monitors and periodically reviews the number of gateways and devices to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zero Trust Device Segmentation is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-device-segmentation-logs","lastmod":"2025-12-17T06:46Z","nid":"1514411"} -->
## Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-device-segmentation-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Logs
- Last modified: 2025-12-17T06:46Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation Logs.

By accessing the Zscaler Zero Trust Device Segmentation (formerly Airgap) service, you provide Zscaler the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs. For Device Segmentation, logs are defined as Session Logs and Audit Logs.

- Session Logs: Traffic flow of information related to the sessions originating from endpoints connected to the Zscaler segmentation network.
- Audit Logs: Activity logs of the configuration changes made in the Device Segmentation Admin Portal or API.

Zscaler retains log information for a rolling period of six months during your subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler after the six-month retention cycle.

During the deployment process, you can choose to have the logs stored in either the United States or the European Union.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-gateway-licensing-and-fair-use","lastmod":"2025-11-19T13:12Z","nid":"1529021"} -->
## Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Licensing and Fair Use

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-gateway-licensing-and-fair-use
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Licensing & Fair Use > Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Licensing and Fair Use
- Last modified: 2025-11-19T13:12Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Licensing and Fair Use.

Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway is a Software as a Service (SaaS) product that is licensed in various ways. This article includes information on licensing types, the license renewal process, and Zscaler’s Fair Use Policy.

## License Types

Zscaler offers the following two types of licenses:

- Monthly Traffic: The total amount of workload traffic that is uploaded and downloaded via the Zero Trust Gateway in a calendar month. The monthly traffic is measured in gigabytes (GB) and is subscribed accordingly. The monthly traffic component also includes entitlement to Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) platforms for workloads. For every 1 GB of ZIA and ZPA egress traffic, you receive an additional 10 GB total for Layer-4 policy enforcement for east-west and ingress traffic flows.
- Gateway Instance: A subscription license for Zero Trust Gateway instances. Each gateway instance license provides entitlement to a Zero Trust Gateway instance in an Availability Zone in any Amazon Web Services (AWS) region. A minimum of two gateway instances is needed to use a gateway in an AWS region.

Ensure that you order the correct amount of monthly traffic and gateway instances. If you require additional monthly traffic or gateway instances, contact Zscaler Sales or your Channel Partner. Zscaler periodically reviews the amount of monthly traffic and gateway instances to ensure license compliance.

The usage of Zero Trust Gateway is expected to be in accordance with the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-gateway-logs","lastmod":"2025-04-29T09:16Z","nid":"1529022"} -->
## Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/logs-fair-use/zscaler-zero-trust-gateway-logs
- Product: Logs & Fair Use
- Path: Logs & Fair Use > Logs & Data > Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Logs
- Last modified: 2025-04-29T09:16Z
- Summary: Information about Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway Logs.

Zscaler Zero Trust Gateway logs are defined as Session Logs, Tunnel Logs, DNS Logs, and Audit Logs. To learn more, see [About Insights Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/about-insights-logs).

- Session Logs: Traffic flow of information related to the sessions originating from your cloud workloads. To learn more, see [Session Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/session-insights-logs-filters) and [Session Insights Log: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/session-insights-logs-columns).
- Tunnel Logs: Information related to the connectivity from the gateway to the Zscaler cloud. To learn more, see [Tunnel Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/zia-tunnel-insights-logs-filters) and [Tunnel Insights Logs: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/tunnel-insights-logs-columns).
- DNS Logs: Information related to the destination domains and the DNS responses for those domains. To learn more, see [DNS Insights Logs: Filters](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/dns-insights-logs-filters) and [DNS Insights Logs: Columns](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/dns-insights-logs-columns).
- Audit Logs: Activity logs of the configuration changes made via the Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal or API for Cloud Connector or Branch Connector. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/about-audit-logs).

Your logs for Zero Trust Gateway are retained by Zscaler for a rolling six month period during your subscription. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler after the six month retention cycle.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-account-settings","lastmod":"2026-07-24T02:41Z","nid":"1540738"} -->
## About Account Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-account-settings
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Getting Started > Management Portal > About Account Settings
- Last modified: 2026-07-24T02:41Z
- Summary: Information on the Settings page and its features in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Account settings allow you to manage your account and customize various aspects of your account. You can modify or view your account settings from the Settingspage in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Account settings provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Update and manage your account details such as email address, contact information, logo, reset password etc.
- Manage subscription agreements, notifications and authentication.

## About the Settings Page

On the Settings page, you can do the following:

1. View your account information:

- The partner account name.
- **Partner ID**: The ID generated when you created your account with Zscaler.
- The status of your account.
- **Partner Type**: The type of partner account.

1. [Update your account logo.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/updating-partner-account-logo)
2. [Modify your account settings.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/modifying-your-account-settings)
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-admins-management-portal-partners","lastmod":"2026-06-17T00:41Z","nid":"1540749"} -->
## About Admins in the Management Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-admins-management-portal-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Admin Management > About Admins in the Management Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-06-17T00:41Z
- Summary: Information on Admins in the Management Portal for Partners.

Zscaler partners can create admin users with different permissions to manage intended tenants or tenant groups on the Management Portal for Partners. You can see all the configured admin users on the Admins page.

The Admins page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View a complete list of admins on your Zscaler partner account.
- Create a new admin.
- Assign or modify an admin's permissions.
- Assign or revoke management of tenants or tenant groups to an admin.

## About the Admins Page

On the Admins page, you can do the following:

1. View a list of configured admins. For each admin, you can see:
  - **Admin Name**: The name of the admin user.
  - **Login ID**: A unique login ID assigned to the admin as per their organization's domain.
  - **Email ID**: The admin's email ID.
  - **Role**: The role assigned to the admin user.
  - **Number of Tenants**: The number of tenants assigned to the admin.
  - **Comments**: Comments about the admin, if any.
  - **Actions**: The options to manage admins (i.e., preview, edit, and delete).
2. [Add a new admin.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/adding-new-admin-management-in-partner-portal)
3. Preview an admin's details.
4. [Edit admins.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)
5. [Delete admins.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)

[Image: Admins page in the Management Portal for Partners]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
