<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-audit-logs-multi-tenant-portal-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:28Z","nid":"1540748"} -->
## About Audit Logs in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-audit-logs-multi-tenant-portal-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > About Audit Logs in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:28Z
- Summary: Information regarding audit logs, including policy and configuration change logs, within the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal.

Zscaler records the login name and IP address of every admin who logs in to the Multi-Tenant Portal and changes configuration settings. Audit logs display an admin's login and logout record (timestamps, actions, IP, etc.) and any configuration change they perform.

Audit logs provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- View changes made in the Multi-Tenant Portal, such as policy template modifications, alterations to the admins or tenant groups, etc.
- View details on all the actions that an admin performs during a login session.
- Detect and investigate suspicious activity, and track unauthorized access to the Multi-Tenant Portal.

## About the Audit Logs Page

On the Audit Logs page, you can do the following:

1. Filter the logs by time range, action, category, sub-category, or result.
2. Search for the logs by resource, login ID, or client IP.
3. Download a CSV file. The times in the CSV file are in PDT.
4. View a list of actions performed in the Multi-Tenant Portal. For each action, you can see:
  - **Timestamp**: The date and time of the admin's action.
  - **Action**: The action performed by the admin in the Multi-Tenant Portal. It can be one of the following:
    - Sign In
    - Sign Out
    - Create
    - Update
    - Delete
  - **Category**: A location within the Multi-Tenant Portal where the action is performed. It can be one of the following:
    - All
    - Login
    - Tenant Group
    - Policy Template
    - Admin Management
    - Partner Settings
  - **Sub-Category**: The subject under the selected category. It can be one of the following:
    - Login
    - Tenant Group
    - Policy Template
    - Partner Settings
    - Roles
    - Admin
  - **Resource**: The item within the selected sub-category. It can be one of the following:
    - Resource
    - Login ID
    - Client IP
  - **Login ID**: The admin's login ID.
  - **Client IP**: The source IP address for the admin.
  - **Interface**: The interface through which the action is performed.
  - **Result**: The outcome of an action, success or failure.
  - **Cloud**: The cloud on which the action is performed.

[Image: Audit Logs Page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-policy-templates","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:00Z","nid":"1540756"} -->
## About Policy Templates

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-policy-templates
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Policy Templates > About Policy Templates
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:00Z
- Summary: Information on Policy Template on the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

A policy template is a customizable document that includes your organization's policies and ensures consistency between policies. Policies of an organization can include purpose, definition, scope, limitations, and actions to be taken. The Zscaler partners can have multiple policy templates created and have them applied to the tenant's account.

Policy templates provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Create a new policy template for individual tenants or tenant groups.
- Edit or delete an existing policy template.
- Edit a policy template on ZIA. For example, policy changes made to Policy Template-1 are visible on the Template-1 account in the ZIA Admin Portal.

## About the Policy Template Page

On the Policy Template page, you can do the following:

1. [Add a policy template](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/adding-policy-templates).
2. View a list of all the policy templates configured. For each policy template, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the policy template.
  - **No. of Tenants**: The total number of tenants assigned with the same policy template.
  - **Description**: The description of the policy template.
  - **Actions**: The actions provisioned for the selected policy template. The actions available are **Edit**, **Delete**, and**Edit Policy Template in ZIA**.
3. [Delete a policy template.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items) Deleting a policy template removes that policy template from the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners database, but the configured template and policies are available in the ZIA policy configurations. When you delete a policy template in the Multi-Tenant Portal, the ZIA admin gets full access to that template (initially accessible as read-only), so that the template under the ZIA tenant can be managed (edit, reorder, or leave as such) by the ZIA admin.
4. [Edit a policy template.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)
5. [Edit a policy template on ZIA](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/edit-policy-templates-zia-admin-portal).

[Image: About Policy Template in the Multi-Tenant Portal Page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-roles-multi-tenant-portal-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:41Z","nid":"1540753"} -->
## About Roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-roles-multi-tenant-portal-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Role Management > About Roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:41Z
- Summary: Information on roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners provides a Role-based Access Control (RBAC) feature that allows you to create and customize admin role templates as required.

A role template in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners can allow or restrict access to different function modules of the portal as defined by the admin.

For example, a role template can provide full access to the Tenants page but view-only access to Policy Templates. Another role template can provide permissions to edit admins while not giving permissions to view the tenants, and so on.

The Roles page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Create customized RBAC templates for different function modules in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.
- Create customized RBAC templates for products managed by the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.
- Assign role templates to different admin users as needed.

## About the Roles Page

On the Roles page, you can do the following:

1. View a list of roles in your customer account. For each role, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the role.
  - **Full Access**: The sections an admin user with this role can access fully.
  - **View-Only Access**: The sections an admin user with this role can view but not edit.
  - **Description**: The description of the role.
  - **Actions**: The actions an admin user with full access can take (e.g., edit or delete a role).
2. [Add a new role.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/managing-roles-management-portal-partners)
3. Preview super admin's permissions.
4. [Edit roles.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/managing-roles-management-portal-partners)
5. [Delete roles.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/managing-roles-management-portal-partners)

[Image: The Roles page in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-scopes","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:45Z","nid":"1540897"} -->
## About Scopes

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-scopes
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Role Management > About Scopes
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:45Z
- Summary: Information on Scopes in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Scopes help you better manage your tenants and admins in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners. Zscaler partners can create unique scopes that cover multiple tenants across various clouds and assign them to specific admins as required. Admins can view and manage tenants solely within their assigned scope.

For partners who have migrated to Authentication Service, the Authentication Service Admin Portal manages all scope and role assignments. To assign scopes and roles to admins, go to Administration > Entitlements > Partner Portal in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.

The Scopes page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Create a new scope with multi-tenant and multi-cloud settings.
- View and manage existing scopes.

## About the Scopes Page

On the Scopes page, you can do the following:

1. View the list of scopes in your partner account. For each scope, you can see:
  - **Scope Name**: The name of the scope.
  - **No. of Tenants**: Number of tenants covered by the scope.
  - **Actions**: Edit and delete options for each scope.
2. [Create a new scope.](https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/adding-new-scope)
3. [Edit a scope](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items).
4. [Delete a scope](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items).

[Image: The Scopes page in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-tenant-groups","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:13Z","nid":"1540746"} -->
## About Tenant Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-tenant-groups
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Tenant Management > About Tenant Groups
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:13Z
- Summary: Information on Tenant Groups in the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

In the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners, you can group tenants across clouds and industries. This feature facilitates easy tenant management as well as policy deployment to multiple tenants across clouds.

The Tenant Groups page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View a complete list of tenant groups.
- Deploy policies to multiple tenants across clouds more efficiently.
- Assign tenant groups to admin users for easy tenant management.

## About Tenant Groups Page

On the Tenant Groups page (Tenant > Tenant Groups), you can do the following:

1. View a list of all tenant groups. For each group, you can view:
  - **Name**: The name of the group.
  - **Policy Template**: The linked policy's name. A group can only be provisioned in one policy template.
  - **Number of Tenants**: The number of tenants in a group.
  - **Description**: The group's description.
  - **Action**: The action (Edit or Delete) you can take on the group.
2. [View a tenant group's details.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/viewing-tenant-details)
3. [Create a tenant group.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/configuring-tenant-groups)
4. [Edit a tenant group.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)
5. [Delete a tenant group.](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)
6. Go back to the [Tenants](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-tenants-management-portal-partners) tab.

[Image: Getting familiar with the Tenant Group page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/about-tenants-multi-tenant-portal","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:07Z","nid":"1540741"} -->
## About Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/about-tenants-multi-tenant-portal
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Tenant Management > About Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:07Z
- Summary: Information on Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

Zscaler partners can view and manage all tenants associated with their customer account from the Tenants page on the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

The Tenant page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View a complete list of customers managed by you.
- See each customer's licenses, subscription renewal information, and other details.

## About the Tenants Page

On the Tenants page, you can do the following:

1. View a list of all tenants linked to a customer account. For each tenant, you can view:
  - **Tenant Name**: The name of the tenant. You can also view the details of a particular tenant by clicking on their name. To learn more, see [Viewing Tenant's Details](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/viewing-tenant-details).
  - **Organization ID**: The ID assigned to the tenant.
  - **Customer Name**: The name of the customer.
  - **Customer ID**: The ID assigned to the customer.
  - **Domains**: The domains associated with the tenant account.
  - **Subscription**: The subscription configured for the tenant.
  - **Policy Template**: The policy templates the tenant is provisioned.
  - **Tenant Group**: The group the tenant belongs to.
  - **Status**: The status of the tenant account.
2. View the tenant account details.
3. Filter to view the tenants based on the cloud they are provisioned on.
4. View tenants with disabled accounts.
5. Filter and search for tenants based on the customer name, customer ID, tenant name or domain, or organization ID.
6. Search for a customer or tenant.
7. Go to the [Tenant Groups](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-tenant-groups) tab.

[Image: Getting familiar with the Tenants page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/accessing-and-navigating-zscaler-multi-tenant-portal-for-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-24T02:36Z","nid":"1540735"} -->
## Accessing and Navigating the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/accessing-and-navigating-zscaler-multi-tenant-portal-for-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Getting Started > Accessing and Navigating the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-24T02:36Z
- Summary: First-time login information to the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

This article covers the following topics to help you get started with the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners:

- Accessing the Multi-Tenant Portal
- Navigating within the Multi-Tenant Portal
- Maintenance and Upgrade

Zscaler Support configures a default admin role, which has access to all the functions in the Multi-Tenant Portal, and sends you an email requesting the password be reset for that role. After you reset that password, you can access the [Multi-Tenant Portal](https://partners.zscalerscm.net/#/login).

For partners who have moved to Authentication Service, the login page redirects to the Authentication Service SSO screen after the Login ID screen. To learn more, see [Accessing and Navigating the Authentication Service Landing Page](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/accessing-and-navigating-zidentity-landing-page).

To access the Multi-Tenant Portal:

1. Enter your **Login ID** and **Password**.
2. Select **Remember my Login ID**if you want the Multi-Tenant Portal to remember your username the next time you log in.
3. From the drop-down menu, select the language in which you want to use the portal. By default, **English (US)**is selected.
4. Click **Sign In**.

[Image: Sign In page for Multi-Tenant Portal]

You cannot access the Multi-Tenant Portal during an upgrade. A maintenance page is displayed during the active upgrade period.

The Multi-Tenant Portal has the following items in the left-side navigation:

- Tenant
- Roles
- Scopes
- Admins
- Authentication Service
- Policy Templates
- Audit Logs
- Settings
- Account
- Sign Out

[Image: Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners' Side Nav Bar]

Click the **Tenant** icon to view all the tenants associated with your account. You can also create and manage tenant groups. To learn more, see [About Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-tenants-management-portal-partners) and [About Tenant Groups](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-tenant-groups).

Click the **Roles** icon to view and manage admin roles for your account. To learn more, see [About Roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-roles-management-portal-partners).

Click the **Scopes**icon to view and manage scopes for tenants and admins. To learn more, see [About Scopes](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-scopes).

Click the**Admins** icon to view the admins configured for the Multi-Tenant Portal. To learn more, see[About Admins in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-admins-management-portal-partners).

Click the **Authentication Service** icon to access the partner Authentication Service Admin Portal. This icon is only visible to users who have migrated to Authentication Service and possess the necessary permissions to access and manage the Multi-Tenant Portal within Authentication Service. To learn more, see [Accessing and Navigating the Authentication Service Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/accessing-and-navigating-zidentity-admin-portal).

Click the**Policy Templates** icon to view and manage policy templates for the tenants. To learn more, see [About Policy Templates](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-policy-templates).

Click the **Audit Logs** icon to view a list of actions performed in the Multi-Tenant Portal. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-audit-logs-management-portal-partners).

Click the **Settings** icon to view or modify your partner account settings. To learn more, see [About Account Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-account-settings).

Click the **Account**icon to see your account information, such as your partner account name and the admin user ID.

Click the **Sign Out** icon to sign out of the Multi-Tenant Portal when you are done. If you are inactive for 15 minutes, the Multi-Tenant Portal automatically logs you out.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/adding-new-admin-multi-tenant-portal-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:32Z","nid":"1540750"} -->
## Adding a New Admin in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/adding-new-admin-multi-tenant-portal-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Admin Management > Adding a New Admin in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:32Z
- Summary: How to create admin users in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Zscaler partners can create admin users with different permissions to manage intended tenants or tenant groups on the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

To add a new admin user:

1. Go to **Admins** and click **Add Admin**. The **Add Admin** window appears.
2. In the **Add Admin** window: See image.
  - **Login ID**: Enter a login ID for the admin user. Select a domain name from the list of domains configured for your organization. A unique login ID is created for the admin in an email format with the information that you provide here.
  - **Admin Name**: Enter a name for the admin to be associated with the login ID.
  - **Email ID**: Enter the email ID of the admin user.
  - **Role**: Select a role template for the admin.
  - **Cloud**: Select a cloud.
  - **Tenants**: Select tenants from the respective cloud.
  - **Comments**: Enter additional notes or information. The description cannot exceed 10,240 characters.
  - **Password**: Enter the password to be set for the login ID.
  - **Confirm Password**: Retype the password for confirmation.
3. Click **Save**.

[Image: Adding a new admin in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/adding-new-scope","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:47Z","nid":"1540899"} -->
## Adding a New Scope

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/adding-new-scope
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Role Management > Adding a New Scope
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:47Z
- Summary: Information on how to add a new scope in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

Zscaler partners can create scopes that encompass multiple tenants and clouds in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners. These scopes are assigned to one or more admins in the Authentication Service Admin Portal as required.

To create a scope:

1. Go to the **Scopes** page.
2. Click **Add Scope**. The **Add Scope** window appears.
3. In the **Add Scope** window: See image.
  - **Scope Name**: Enter a name for the scope.
  - **Cloud**: Select the cloud on which the tenant is provisioned.
  - **Tenants**: Select tenants from the drop-down menu. The list of tenants available is based on the cloud selected.
  - **Add Cloud**: Click this button to add another cloud. You can add tenants under each selected cloud.
4. Click **Save**.

[Image: The Add Scope window]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/adding-policy-templates","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:58Z","nid":"1540755"} -->
## Adding Policy Templates

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/adding-policy-templates
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Policy Templates > Adding Policy Templates
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:58Z
- Summary: Information on how to add a policy template in the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

You can add a policy template for tenants or tenant groups from the [Policy Template page](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-policy-templates) in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners. A tenant or tenant group can be associated to only one policy template.

To add a policy template:

1. Go to **Policy Template**page.
2. Click **Policy Template.** The **Add Policy Template** window appears.
3. In the **Add Policy Template** window: See image.
  - **Name**: Enter a name for the policy template.
  - **Cloud**: Select the cloud on which the tenant is provisioned.
  - **Tenants**: Select tenants from the drop-down menu. The list of tenants available is based on the cloud selected.
  - **Add Cloud**: Click **Add Cloud**to add another cloud. You can add tenants under the selected cloud.
  - **Tenant Groups**: Select tenant groups from the drop-down menu.
  - **Allow Policy Rule Reorder**: This option is disabled by default and hence the policy is enforced at top priority. If enabled, the ZIA Admin Portal admins can change the order of the policy in the **Rule Order**option (Policy > URL & Cloud App Control > Edit URL Filtering Rule).
  - **Description**: (Optional) Enter a description for the policy template. The description cannot exceed 256 characters.
4. Click **Save and** **Edit Policies**.

[Image: Adding a policy template on the Multi-Tenant Portal]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/configuring-tenant-groups","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:15Z","nid":"1540747"} -->
## Configuring Tenant Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/configuring-tenant-groups
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Tenant Management > Configuring Tenant Groups
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:15Z
- Summary: How to configure and manage tenant groups in the Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

You can configure tenant groups to boost easy tenant management and to apply security policies to multiple tenants at once. You can create, view, or manage tenant groups based on your organization’s needs.

Only an admin with permission to manage tenants can create, view, or modify tenant groups.

## Creating and Viewing a Tenant Group

- Creating a Tenant Group
- Viewing a Tenant Group's details

To create a new tenant group:

1. Go to **Tenants > Tenant Groups.**
2. Click on the **Add Tenant Group** button. The **Add Tenant Group** window appears.
3. In the **Add Tenant Group** window: See image.
  - **Name**: Enter a name for the group.
  - **Cloud**: Select a cloud.
  - **Tenants**: Select tenants from the cloud.
  - **Description**: Add a description, if you want.
4. Click **Save**.

To learn how to apply policy to a tenant group, see [About Policy Templates](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-policy-templates).

[Image: Add Tenant Group window]

To see the details of a particular tenant group,

1. Go to **Tenants > Tenant Groups**.
2. Click on the group's name. On the Tenant group details page, you can see: See image.
  - **Tenant Name**: The name of the tenants in the group.
  - **Organization ID**: The organization ID of the particular tenant.
  - **Customer name**: The name of the customer the tenant comes under.
  - **Customer ID**: The customer ID.
  - **Domains**: The domains registered by the tenant.
  - **Subscription**: The subscription plan of the tenant.
  - **Policy Templates**: The policies provisioned to the tenant.
  - **Clouds**: The clouds provisioned to the tenant.
  - **Status**: The tenant's status (Active or Disabled).

[Image: Viewing a Tenant Group's details]

## Editing Tenant Groups

To edit an existing tenant group:

1. Go to**Tenants > Tenant Groups.**
2. Click on the **Edit** icon next to the group.
3. Modify the fields you want to change: See image.
  - **Name**: The name of the tenant group.
  - **Clouds**: The clouds provisioned to the tenant group.
  - **Tenants**: The tenants in the group.
  - **Description**: The group's description.
4. Click **Save**.

[Image: Edit Tenant Group window]

## Adding Policy Templates to Tenant Groups

To assign security policy templates to a tenant group:

1. Go to **Policy Templates**.
2. Click on the **Edit** icon next to the policy you want to assign. The **Edit Policy** **Template** window appears.
3. In the**Edit Policy Template** window, add the tenant group under **Tenant Groups**. See image.
4. Click **Save and Sync**.

[Image: Edit Policy Template window]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/edit-policy-templates-zia-admin-portal","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:02Z","nid":"1540757"} -->
## Edit Policy Templates in the ZIA Admin Portal

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/edit-policy-templates-zia-admin-portal
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Policy Templates > Edit Policy Templates in the ZIA Admin Portal
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:02Z
- Summary: Information on how to edit policy template on ZIA Admin Portal

You can edit a policy template with different policies on the ZIA Admin Portal from the [Policy Template page](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-policy-templates). You can save and synchronize policies for multiple tenants under multiple clouds.

To edit a policy template on ZIA:

1. Go to the **Policy Template**page.
2. Click the **Edit Policy Template on ZIA**icon to redirect to the ZIA Admin Portal. See image.
3. On the ZIA Admin Portal page, you can:
  - Add URL Filtering Rule
  - Add URL Categories
  - [Edit URL Filtering and URL Categories](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)
  - [Delete URL Filtering and URL Categories](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/editing-deleting-items)

To learn more, see [Add URL Filtering Rule](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/configuring-url-filtering-policy), [About URL Filtering](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-filtering), [Add URL Categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/configuring-custom-url-categories), and [About URL Categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories).

[Image: Policy Template Page]

You can add a new URL Filtering rule, copy an existing rule, or change its settings.

To add a URL Filtering Rule:

1. Go to**Policy**>**URL & Cloud App Control**.
2. Click **Add URL Filtering Rule**. You can also copy an existing rule by clicking the **Duplicate**icon. The **Add URL Filtering Rule** window appears. The fields such as Rule Label, Source IP Groups, Users, Groups, Departments, Locations, Location Groups, Devices, Device Groups, Device Trust Level, and HTTP Header Profiles in the URL Filtering Rule are not synchronized with the user and are not editable.
3. In the **Add URL Filtering Rule** window: See image.
  - **Rule Order**: Select the rule order from the drop-down menu. Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on), and the rule order reflects this rule's place in the order. This option is only editable if you enable **Allow Policy Rule Reorder**in the Multi-Tenant Portal (Policy Template > Add Policy Template > Allow Policy Rule Reorder).
  - **Rule Name**: Enter a unique name for the rule or use the default name.
  - **Rule Status**: An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.
  - **URL Categories**: Select the URL categories, or search for the categories from the drop-down menu.
  - **Request Methods**:Select the required HTTP request methods for which you want to apply the rule. You can also search for a specific HTTP request method. The following HTTP request methods are available: This criterion is mandatory, and you must select a value for it.
    - **OPTIONS**: Requests for information about communication options for the specified resource.
    - **GET**: Requests for and retrieves the specified resource from the server.
    - **HEAD**: Requests for and retrieves only the header information from the server. This is similar to the `GET` request but does not retrieve a response body from the server.
    - **POST**: Requests the specified resource to accept the data enclosed in the request message and processes the data according to the resource’s semantics.
    - **PUT**: Requests the specified resource to create or replace the data enclosed in the request message.
    - **DELETE**: Requests the server to delete the specified resource.
    - **TRACE**: Requests a remote loop-back of the message along the path to the target resource. This method is useful for diagnostic purposes.
    - **CONNECT**: Requests an HTTP Proxy server to tunnel the TCP connection with the client.
    - **OTHER**: All other request methods.
  - **Time**: Select **Always** to apply this rule to all [time intervals](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/how-do-i-define-time-intervals), or select up to two time intervals.
  - **Protocols**: Select the protocols to which the rule applies. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.
    - **DNS Over HTTPS**: URLs that use DNS Over HTTPS.
    - **FTP over HTTP**: URLs that use FTP over HTTP.
    - **HTTP**: URLs that use HTTP.
    - **HTTP Proxy**: URLs that use the HTTP Proxy server when the client is configured in explicit proxy mode, which makes the HTTP `CONNECT` request to the proxy server to tunnel the TCP connections. The tunnel is typically set up when using TLS.
    - **HTTPS**: URLs that use HTTP encrypted by TLS/SSL.
    - **Native FTP**: URLs that use FTP.
    - **SSL**: URLs that use SSL encryption and haven't been decrypted. For example, URLs you've [exempted from SSL inspection](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-ssl-inspection#configure-ssl-inspection-policy).
    - **Tunnel**: Encrypted URLs that use an unidentified protocol. For example, URLs from tunneling applications such as Telnet or SSH that are encapsulated in HTTP or HTTPS.
    - **Tunnel SSL**: Undecodable protocol within an SSL connection.
    - **WebSocket**: URLs that use WebSocket.
    - **WebSocket SSL**: URLs that use WebSocket within an SSL connection.
  - **User Agent**: Select any number of user agents to which the rule applies. You can also search for an agent. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.
  - **Enable Rule Expiration**: Enable this option to set a validity period for the rule.
    - **Start Date and Time**: Select a start date and time. The rule is valid starting on this date and time.
    - **End Date and Time**: Select an end date and time. The rule ceases to be valid on this date and time.
    - **Time Zone**: Select the time zone in which the rule is valid.
  - Select the **Action** for the rule.
  - **Description**:(Optional) Enter additional notes or information. The description cannot exceed 10,240 characters.
4. Click **Save & Sync.**

- **Allow**:Select this to allow access to all sites in the selected [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories).
  - **Daily Bandwidth Quota**: (Optional) The daily bandwidth limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. To enforce the quota on specific users, groups, or departments, Zscaler recommends that IP surrogacy is used to aid in identification. To learn more, see [About Surrogate IP](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/what-surrogate-ip). In addition, if you have different policies for different groups, Zscaler recommends that you create a catch-all “any” user policy with a higher limit. This catch-all policy should only apply to unidentified users (do not use “any” user to define “all remaining groups or departments”). This is helpful if you encounter a scenario where there are a high number of unidentified users as the users have a higher combined limit, facilitating continuity of service. If a user comes from a [known location](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-locations), the quota is reset at midnight based on the location time zone; for remote users, the quota is reset based on the organization's time zone. The minimum value you can enter is 10 MB and the maximum value is 100,000 MB.
  - **Daily Time Quota**: (Optional) The daily time limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. The session idle times are ignored. The minimum value you can enter is 15 minutes and the maximum value is 600 minutes.
- **Caution**: Select to display an End User Notification (EUN) that cautions users before allowing them access to the site. When you select this value, the service can either display the default EUN or redirect users to an EUN that is hosted on the site you specify in the **Redirect URL** field. You can select this action for only one of the following request methods: **CONNECT**, **GET**, or **HEAD**.
  - **Daily Bandwidth Quota**: (Optional) The daily bandwidth limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. To enforce the quota on specific users, groups, or departments, Zscaler recommends that IP surrogacy is used to aid in identification. To learn more, see [About Surrogate IP](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/what-surrogate-ip). In addition, if you have different policies for different groups, Zscaler recommends that you create a catch-all “any” user policy with a higher limit. This catch-all policy should only apply to unidentified users (do not use “any” user to define “all remaining groups or departments”). This is helpful if you encounter a scenario where there are a high number of unidentified users as the users have a higher combined limit, facilitating continuity of service. If a user comes from a [known location](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-locations), the quota is reset at midnight based on the location time zone; for remote users, the quota is reset based on the organization's time zone. The minimum value you can enter is 10 MB and the maximum value is 100,000 MB.
  - **Daily Time Quota**: (Optional) The daily time limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. The session idle times are ignored. The minimum value you can enter is 15 minutes and the maximum value is 600 minutes.
  - **Redirect URL**:(Optional) Leave the field blank to display the service's default [notification](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-acceptable-use-policy-and-end-user-notifications). If you want to redirect users to a site that hosts a custom notification, enter the site URL. The URL requires the schema (for example, https://redirect.company.com/redirectpage.cgi) and can be HTTP or HTTPS. During the redirection, all query parameters are sent to the external site to enable notification customization.
- **Block**:Select to block access to all sites in the selected URL categories. If you enable this option, the EUN provides the users with a link to access the blocked page. The users are then prompted to enter their single sign-on credentials or hosted database credentials based on the [Enable Identity-based Block Override](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/configuring-advanced-url-policy-settings#Enable-block-override) settings. The authenticated users are allowed to access the blocked page only during their current browser session. They must re-authenticate if they try to access it through another browser session.
  - **Allow Override** appears when you select **Block**. Enable this option to allow specific [users](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/adding-user-account) or [groups](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/how-do-i-add-group) to access the blocked site.
    - **Override Users**:Select **Any** to allow the override to all users, or select up to 32 users. You can search for users or click the **Add**icon to add a new user. You cannot select users if you want to select override groups.
    - **Override Groups**:Select **Any** to allow the override to all groups, or you can select up to 32 groups. You can search for groups or click the **Add**icon to add a new group. You cannot select groups if you want to select override users. The default limit of users and groups is expandable. To increase the limits, please contact your sales or accounts team.
  - **Redirect URL**:(Optional) If you choose not to allow an override, the service blocks access and displays a notification. The service can either display the default EUN or redirect users to an EUN that is hosted on the site you specify in the **Redirect URL** field. Leave the field blank to display the service’s default [notification](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-acceptable-use-policy-and-end-user-notifications). If you want to redirect users to a site that hosts a custom notification, enter the site URL. The URL requires the schema (for example, https://redirect.company.com/redirectpage.cgi) and can be HTTP or HTTPS. During the redirection, all query parameters are sent to the external site to enable notification customization.
  - **Capture**: Appears when you select **Block** while Traffic Capture is enabled. Enable this option to capture and store traffic in packet capture (PCAP) files. To learn more, see [Configuring Traffic Capture Settings](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/configuring-traffic-capture).
- **Isolate**: Select to isolate all the traffic that matches the URL filtering rule through a remote browser. To learn more, see [What Is Isolation?](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-cloud-browser-isolation). This action is available only if Isolation is enabled for your organization.
  - **Isolation Profile**: Appears when you select **Isolate**. You can choose the Isolation profiles to which the rule applies. Ensure you [create Isolation profiles](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/creating-isolation-profile-cloud-browser-isolation) for your organization.
  - **Daily Bandwidth Quota**: (Optional) The daily bandwidth limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. To enforce the quota on specific users, groups, or departments, Zscaler recommends that IP surrogacy is used to aid in identification. To learn more, see [About Surrogate IP](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/what-surrogate-ip). In addition, if you have different policies for different groups, Zscaler recommends that you create a catch-all “any” user policy with a higher limit. This catch-all policy should only apply to unidentified users (do not use “any” user to define “all remaining groups or departments”). This is helpful if you encounter a scenario where there are a high number of unidentified users as the users have a higher combined limit, facilitating continuity of service. If a user comes from a [known location](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-locations), the quota is reset at midnight based on the location time zone; for remote users, the quota is reset based on the organization's time zone. The minimum value you can enter is 10 MB and the maximum value is 100,000 MB.
  - **Daily Time Quota**: (Optional) The daily time limit allowed for uploading and/or downloading data from the [URL categories](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/about-url-categories) before the websites are blocked. The session idle times are ignored. The minimum value you can enter is 15 minutes and the maximum value is 600 minutes.

[Image: Add URL Filtering Rule window]

You can add a new URL category, view an existing URL category, or change its settings.

To add a custom URL category:

1. Go to **Administration**>**URL Categories**.
2. Click **Add URL Category**. The **Add URL Category**window appears.
3. In the **Add URL Category**window: See image.
  - **Name**: Enter a name for the new category. Category names can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, hyphens, dots, parentheses, and spaces.
  - **URL Super Category**: Select the URL super category that you want the custom category to belong to from the drop-down menu.
  - **Administrator Operational Scope**: Select the operational scope for this category. This option is only available for categories where the URL Super Category is **User-Defined**. You can select multiple operational scopes and when there is more than one scope, OR logic is used to find a match. Select from the following scopes: If there are any operational scopes that you don't see, they are not part of your administrative operational scope. You can only delete a custom category that belongs to the **User-Defined**URL Super Category if your administrator scope is identical to the scope of the custom category.
    - **Any**: Any admin can manage this category. If your organization does not have granular access requirements for custom URL categories, select **Any** as the scope. You can then control which admins are able to manage custom categories through admin roles.
    - **Organization**: Admins whose scope is Organization can manage this category.
    - **Location Group**: Admins with one or more of the selected location groups in their scope can manage this category.
    - **Location**: Admins with one or more of the selected locations in their scope can manage this category. Admins that have an operational scope over location groups that include one or more of the selected locations can also manage this category. However, they cannot change the operational scope of the category.
    - **Department**: Admins with one or more of the selected departments in their operational scope can manage this category.
  - **Custom URLs**:Enter the URLs or IP addresses you want to add to this custom category and click **Add Items**. This field supports IPv6 addresses either in full or short form (e.g., 2041:0000:140f:0000:0000:0000:875b:131b or 2041:0000:140f::875b:131b). Add URLs or IP addresses to this field if you want to override the category or create your own denylist or allowlist of URLs or IP addresses. URLs or IP addresses added to Custom URLs do not remain mapped to the category in the Zscaler URL database, also called the parent category. So these URLs or IP addresses are covered by policies that reference this specific custom category, but not by policies that reference their parent category. For example, if you enter www.amazon.com, then this site is no longer covered by policies that reference its parent URL category (Online Shopping). To add multiple entries, press `Enter` after each entry. For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page; filter the list by searching for a word, phrase, or number contained in an item; and remove the first 25,000 items from the list (**Remove 25K Items**) or only items from a specific page (**Remove Page**). If you select **Remove 25K Items** or **Remove Page**, a confirmation window appears. To learn how to find the parent category of a given URL, see [Looking up URLs in the ZIA Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/lookup-urls-admin-portal). For guidance on entering URLs, see the [URL format guidelines](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/url-format-guidelines).
  - **URLs Retaining Parent Category**: Enter the URLs or IP addresses you want to add to this custom category and click **Add Items**. This field supports IPv6 addresses either in full or short form (e.g., 2041:0000:140f:0000:0000:0000:875b:131b or 2041:0000:140f::875b:131b). URLs retaining parent category remain mapped to their parent category. So these URLs or IP addresses are covered by policies that reference the parent category and this custom category. For example, if you enter www.amazon.com, then this site is covered by policies that reference this custom category and its parent URL category (Online Shopping). To add multiple entries, press `Enter` after each entry. For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page; filter the list by searching for a word, phrase, or number contained in an item; and remove the first 25,000 items from the list (**Remove 25K Items**) or only items from a specific page (**Remove Page**). If you select **Remove 25K Items** or **Remove Page**, a confirmation window appears. If you add already categorized URLs or IP addresses to the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category in the **URLs retaining parent category** field, the system only categorizes URLs or IP addresses under the pre-existing URL category and not under the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category. For example, if you add www.blogs.com belonging to the **Blogs** category to the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category in the **URLs retaining parent category** field, and if you had a policy that blocked the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category, then www.blogs.com is not blocked as it's categorized under the pre-existing **Blogs** category and not under the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category.
  - **Custom Keywords**: Enter keywords that you want to add to this custom category and click **Add Items**. To add multiple entries, press `Enter` after each entry. For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page; filter the list by searching for a word, phrase, or number contained in an item; and remove all items from the list (**Remove All**) or only items from a specific page (**Remove Page**). If you select **Remove All** or **Remove Page**, a confirmation window appears. URLs that match the keywords are added to the custom category but are not retained under their original parent category. For example, if you create a custom URL category that includes "gambling" as a custom keyword, a site like www.gambling.com is only covered by policies that reference this custom category. It's not covered by policies that reference its parent URL category (Gambling). Policies including custom keywords trigger if the keyword is a full or partial match of the URI. For example, if you had a policy that blocked a URL category that included "gambling," then www.gambling101.com and www.gambling.com would both be blocked. In addition, as custom keywords apply to the entire URI, if you go to www.google.com and search for "gambling," the search results are blocked since the word "gambling" appears in the URI (https://www.google.com/search?q=*gambling*&oq=*gambling*&aqs=chrome..69i57j0l4.2767j0j8&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8). Custom keywords must be between 3 and 255 characters.
  - **Keywords Retaining Parent Category**: Enter the keywords you want to add to this custom category and click **Add Items**. To add multiple entries, press **Enter** after each entry. For item lists, you can view up to 500 items on a page; filter the list by searching for a word, phrase, or number contained in an item; and remove all items from the list (**Remove All**) or only items from a specific page (**Remove Page**). If you select **Remove All** or **Remove Page**, a confirmation window appears. URLs that match the keywords are added to the custom category and also retained under their original parent category. For example, if you create a custom URL category that includes "gambling" as a keyword retaining parent category, a site like www.gambling.com is covered by policies that reference this custom category as well as by policies that reference its parent URL category (Gambling). Policies, including keywords retaining the parent category, trigger if the keyword is a full or partial match of the URI. Keywords retaining the parent category must be between 3 and 255 characters. Adding keywords in the URLs belonging to the **Miscellaneous or Unknown** category to the **Keywords retaining parent category** in a URL category only categorizes the URLs under the respective URL category and not under **Miscellaneous or Unknown**.
  - **Description**: (Optional) Enter additional notes or information. The description cannot exceed 256 characters.
4. Click **Save & Sync**.

[Image: Add URL Category window]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## Editing or Deleting Items

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/editing-deleting-items
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Getting Started > Management Portal > Editing or Deleting Items
- Last modified: 2026-07-28T01:07Z
- Summary: How to edit, delete, or duplicate items in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

You can edit or delete the configured items in your Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal account. For example, you can edit or delete the configured users, or policy templates.

## Editing Items

To edit items:

1. Go to the item you want to edit.
2. Click the **Edit** icon, as shown in the following example.

1. Make the changes and click **Save**or **Save & Sync**.

## Deleting Items

To delete items with the Edit icon:

1. Go to the item you want to delete.
2. Click the**Edit**icon.
3. Click **Delete & Sync**. See image.

To delete items with the Delete icon:

1. Go to the item you want to delete.
2. Click the **Delete**icon. [Image: Delete icon]
3. Read the warning message that appears. The following is an example. See image.
4. Click **Confirm**to delete the item.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/managing-roles-multi-tenant-portal-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-29T08:40Z","nid":"1540754"} -->
## Managing Roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/managing-roles-multi-tenant-portal-partners
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Administration > Role Management > Managing Roles in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T08:40Z
- Summary: How to edit or delete a role in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

The Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners allows you to create your own customized [admin role templates](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-roles-management-portal-partners). You can further edit or delete existing role templates in your Zscaler partner account.

## Adding a New Role

To create a new role template:

1. Go to **Roles**.
2. Click on the **Add Role** button. The **Add Role**window appears.
3. In the **Add Role** window, enter the following details: See image.
  - **Role Name**: The name of the role.
  - **Permissions**: Define permissions for different sections.
  - **Description**: Add a description for the role.
4. Click **Save**.

[Image: Adding a new role in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners]

## Editing Roles

To edit a role template:

1. Go to **Roles**.
2. Click the **Edit** icon. The **Edit Role** window appears.
3. Modify the permissions. See image.
4. Click **Save**.

[Image: Editing a role in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners]

## Deleting Roles

To delete a role template:

1. Go to **Roles**.
2. Click the **Delete** icon.
3. Confirm your decision. See image.
4. Click **Delete**.

[Image: Deleting confirmation modal]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/modifying-your-account-settings","lastmod":"2026-07-28T01:01Z","nid":"1540737"} -->
## Modifying Your Account Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/modifying-your-account-settings
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Getting Started > Management Portal > Modifying Your Account Settings
- Last modified: 2026-07-28T01:01Z
- Summary: Information on how to modify your partner account settings in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

[Account settings](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/about-account-settings) include options that allow you to modify various aspects of your account to suit your preferences (e.g., email notifications, Admin Portal color scheme, logo, etc.). You can make changes to the information associated with your tenant's account.

To modify your partner account settings, you can do the following:

1. In the left-side navigation, go to **Settings**.
2. Make changes to the following fields:

- **End User Subscription Agreement**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Select the end user subscription agreement from the drop-down menu. You can view the selected end user subscription agreement notification for your customers when you log in to the ZIA Admin Portal.
- **Partner UI Logout URL**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--{C}%3C!%2D%2D%7BC%7D%253C!%252D%252Dtd%2520%257Bborder%253A%25201px%2520solid%2520%2523ccc%253B%257Dbr%2520%257Bmso-data-placement%253Asame-cell%253B%257D%252D%252D%253E%2D%2D%3E--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Enter the URL that the tenants see when they log out of the ZIA Admin Portal. This option is only available for white-labeled partners.
- **White Labeling**: Enable this to white label the Admin Portals of your tenant accounts. For example, the partner can configure their logo that the tenants can see at the time of login. The partner can white label the following items:
  - Partner Support
  - Partner CSS Color Scheme (Magenta)
  - Partner UI Logout URL
  - Account Logo
  - Background Color
- **SSO to Tenants' ZIA Admin Portal**: Enable Single Sign-On (SSO) to log in to the tenants' ZIA Admin Portal. You must obtain the SSO certificate from your SAML service provider before enabling this option. If you enable this option, you see the following options:
  - **Certificate (.der)**: Extract and upload the public key from the SSO certificate provided by your SAML service provider. Ensure that the key is binary-encoded using a Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) file before you upload it. The file extension must be .der and should not have other periods (.) in the file name.
  - **Algorithm**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--{C}%3C!%2D%2D%7BC%7D%253C!%252D%252D%257BC%257D%25253C!%25252D%25252Dtd%252520%25257Bborder%25253A%2525201px%252520solid%252520%252523ccc%25253B%25257Dbr%252520%25257Bmso-data-placement%25253Asame-cell%25253B%25257D%25252D%25252D%25253E%252D%252D%253E%2D%2D%3E--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Select the decryption algorithm for the SSO certificate.

You can log in to the tenants' ZIA Admin Portal using the following URLs:

- **Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL/Destination URL**: https://admin.<Cloud_Name>/ssologin.do
- **Entity ID**: https://admin.<Cloud_Name>

See image.

- **SSO to Management Portal for Partners**: Enable SSO to log in to the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners. You must obtain the SSO certificate from your SAML service provider before enabling this option.
  - **Certificate (.pem)**: Upload the SSL public certificate that is used to verify the digital signature of the identity provider (IdP). This is the Base64-encoded PEM format certificate that you downloaded from your IdP. The file extension must be .pem and have no other periods (.) in the file name.

You can log in to the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners using the following URLs:

- **Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL/Destination URL**(Depends on the IdP used (i.e., Okta or Azure)): https://partners.zscalerscm.net/partnersso.do.
- **Entity ID**: As a default value, Zscaler recommends using https://partners.zscalerscm.net/, or you can use any value that is unique to a customer or partner IdP.

See image.

The following explains how the IdP-Initiated SSO works when you enable the SSO to Tenants' ZIA Admin Portal and SSO to Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

**IdP-Initiated SSO Workflow**

An IdP stores and verifies user identity. The users can access various applications and resources securely through the IdP portal. The Multi-Tenant Portal supports IdP-initiated Single Sign-On for which the access and authentication take place through the partner's IdP portal. To learn more, see [Understanding SAML](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/understanding-saml).

The IdP-Initiated workflow is as follows:

- SSO to Tenants' ZIA Admin Portal
- SSO to Management Portal for Partners

See image.

1. Enter the user name and password to log in to the IdP portal (e.g., Azure, Okta, etc.).
2. Click the **SSO to Tenants ZIA Admin Portal**tile in the IdP portal to initiate SSO.

The browser sends a SAML message containing an assertion to the Partner Portal ACS URL.

1. The Partner Portal identifies the user and sends back the signed assertion to the browser.
2. The signed assertion is then received from the Partner Portal and the destination URL (i.e., Admin Portal) is authenticated.

Access to the Tenants' ZIA Admin Portal is complete.

1. Enter the username and password to log in to the IdP portal (eg., Azure, Okta, etc.).
2. Click the **SSO to Management Portal for Partner**tile in the IdP portal to initiate SSO.

The browser sends a SAML message containing an assertion, identifies it, and sends back the signed assertion to https://partners.zscalerscm.net/partnersso.do.

1. The signed assertion is then received and the destination URL is authenticated.

Access to the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners is complete.

- **Internal Domain**: This field shows your internal domain generated when creating your partner account. It is a default domain created for the partner to log in for the first time.
- **Partner Domain**: This field shows your company domain. A partner can have a maximum of 16 domains. Contact Zscaler Support to change or add a partner domain.
- **Color Scheme**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Select the color scheme you want the tenants to see in all the Admin Portals.
- **Partner Support**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Select the support type for your account. Tenants can view this support information in their Admin Portals.
  - **Partner Support Email**: If you select **Email**as the partner support, enter your support email address.
  - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; **Partner Support URL**: If you select **Portal** **URL**as the partner support, enter your support website URL.
- **Reset Password and Send Activation Email**: Select this option to reset your default admin account password. You receive the password reset email link. See image. For partners who have migrated to Authentication Service, the **Reset Password** feature moves under **Administration**in the Authentication Service Admin Portal. To learn more, see [Resetting the Login Credentials or MFA](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/resetting-login-credentials-or-mfa) and [Configuring Security Settings for Users](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/configuring-security-settings-users).
  - **Partner Contact Name**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--{C}%3C!%2D%2Dtd%20%7Bborder%3A%201px%20solid%20%23ccc%3B%7Dbr%20%7Bmso-data-placement%3Asame-cell%3B%7D%2D%2D%3E--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Enter the name of the primary contact person of your partner account.
  - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; **Activation Email Recipient**: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;!--td {border: 1px solid #ccc;}br {mso-data-placement:same-cell;}--&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; Enter the email recipient to receive the password reset link. You can enter multiple recipients. Click **Add Email** after each entry. You can remove all the recipients from the list (**Remove All**) or only specific emails from the list (**X**).

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/updating-partner-account-logo","lastmod":"2026-07-28T01:04Z","nid":"1540739"} -->
## Updating Partner Account Logo

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/updating-partner-account-logo
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Getting Started > Management Portal > Updating Partner Account Logo
- Last modified: 2026-07-28T01:04Z
- Summary: Information on how to update the account logo to a color or an image in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

You can update your account logo or set the background color in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners. Your partner account logo is used for white labeling your tenant's ZIA Admin Portal if you've enabled [white labeling](https://help.zscaler.com/multitenant-partner-portal/modifying-your-account-settings).

To update your account:

- Upload an image for the logo
- Set the background color

To update your account logo with an image:

1. Go to **Settings** page.
2. Click **Upload Logo**. See image.
3. Upload the logo from your local directory. The service supports a logo with the following features:
  - Dimensions of 300 x 220 pixels or less.
  - Size of 10 KB or less.
  - .png, .jpg, or .gif file types.
4. Click **Save**.

To update the background color:

1. Go to **Settings** page.
2. Click **Change Background Color**.
3. Select a color from the list or enter the hexadecimal code of the color you want to update. See image.
4. Click **Save**.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/multi-tenant-portal/viewing-tenant-details","lastmod":"2026-07-29T09:10Z","nid":"1540742"} -->
## Viewing Tenant Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/multi-tenant-portal/viewing-tenant-details
- Product: Multi-Tenant Portal
- Path: Multi-Tenant Portal Help > Tenant Management > Viewing Tenant Details
- Last modified: 2026-07-29T09:10Z
- Summary: Information on viewing the tenant account details of a customer in the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners.

The Tenant Details page shows the account and configuration details of a tenant. This information is view-only and cannot be modified within the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners. If you want to make changes to your configurations, contact Zscaler Support.

To view each tenant's account and configuration details:

1. Go to **Tenants**.
2. From the **Tenant Name** column, click the tenant name for which you want to open the **Tenant Details** page. See image.
3. On the **Tenant Details** page, you can view the following information about your tenant's account: General Account Information; List of Subscriptions; Technical Information; Special Settings; Activation Details; Contact Information; Executive Insights

[Image: Tenant details page]

- The name of the tenant account.
- **Organization ID:** The tenant organization ID.
- The status of the tenant account.
- **View On**: Hover over to access the ZIA Admin Portal of the tenant account. You can also access other admin portals (i.e., Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX), Zscaler Cloud Connector, etc.) if the tenant is provisioned on them.
- **Primary Account Owner**: The owner of the tenant account.
- **Geographical Region**: The geographical region of the tenant.
- **Number of Employees**: The number of employees in the tenant organization.
- **Industry Vertical**: The industry vertical of the tenant organization.
- **HQ Location**: The HQ location of the tenant organization.
- **Account Type**: The type of tenant account.
- **Clouds**: The clouds on which the tenant is provisioned.
- **Account Creation Date**: The tenant account creation date.
- **Last Modified**: The date on which the tenant account was last modified.
- **Tenant Since**: The date since the organization has been Zscaler's tenant.
- **Domains**: The domains of the tenant organization.
- **Internal Domain**: The internal domain. This domain is generated when the tenant account is created with Zscaler.
- **Policy Template**: The policy template applied to the tenant.
- **CMC Hostname**: The CMC Hostname associated with the tenant.
- **Show Partner Logo**: This is a white labeling feature that indicates if the partner logo is enabled or disabled in the admin portals the tenant has access to.

See image.

[Image: Tenant's general information]

- **Subscription Name**: The subscription package for the tenant. You can expand the subscription name to view the list of services offered in the subscription and any additional services, if configured.
- **Bundle/Edition Name**: The name of the bundle or edition.
- **Service Name**: The name of the service in the package. The **ADD-ON** tag beside the service name indicates the additional service included in the package.
- **SKU**: The ID of the service.
- **Status**: Whether the subscription package is on trial, expired, not subscribed, subscribed, or temporarily extended.
- **Start Date**: The start date of the subscription.
- **End Date**: The end date of the subscription.
- **Number of Licenses**: The number of licenses the tenant owns.

See image.

[Image: Tenant's subscriptions]

- **Dedicated Proxy Ports**: The Proxy Ports that are dedicated solely to the tenant.
- **Preferred Nanolog Cluster**: The cluster where the tenant logs are recorded.
- **Sandbox Cluster**: The cluster where files are quarantined and scanned for malicious activities.
- **SMTP Cluster**: The SMTP cluster configured for the tenant.
- **SMCDSS DLP Cluster**: The cluster where the ADP client uploads or downloads the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Schema files for Exact Data Match (EDM).
- **SMAA Servers**: The configured SMAA servers for the tenant account.
- **Source IP-based Load Distribution**: If enabled, indicates that the load distribution is based on source IP rather than source and destination.
- **For allowed Social Media transactions, apply URL Policy**: Indicates whether the URL policy is applied for the allowed social media transactions.
- **Block outbound suspected spam messages**: Indicates whether blocking outbound suspected spam messages is enabled or disabled.
- **Apply location mapping to Global Auth Bypass Traffic**: If enabled, indicates that the Zscaler service marks traffic destined to Global Auth Bypass destinations as the Location.
- **Disable Default Sandbox Rule**: If enabled, indicates that the default Sandbox rules are disabled.
- **Enable Internal IP Features (Sublocations and Surrogate IP)**: If enabled, allows for additional internal IP features in the admin portals.
- **Sandbox Unique Files Analyzed Daily Limit**: The daily file limit for sandbox analysis.
- **Sandbox API File Submission Daily Limit**: The daily API file limit for sandbox analysis.
- **Self-service GRE and IP Provisioning**: If enabled, allows the tenant to provision GRE or IP addresses in the ZIA Admin Portal.
- **Self-provisioned IP Limit**: Indicates the self-provisioning IP limit in the ZIA Admin Portal. The limit is 100, 1,000, 10K, or 100K.
- **Custom URL Category Limit**: Indicates the number of URL categories that can be configured in the ZIA Admin Portal. It can be either 56 or 256.
- **Mobile Admin Service**: Indicates the mobile admin URL for a specific cloud, if configured.
- **DC Exclusion**: If enabled, restricts customer data forwarding to all data centers (DCs) within the country.
- **DC Exclusion for Traffic Forwarding**: When enabled, it shows the Traffic Forwarding Method option for DC Exclusion in the ZIA Admin Portal (Administration > Resources > DC Exclusion > Traffic Forwarding Method).
- **ZPA Tenant**: Indicates if the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) tenant ID is mapped to the ZIA tenant ID.
- **Custom File Type Limit**: Indicates the number of custom file types that can be created for file type policies in the ZIA Admin Portal. It can either be 512, 1,024, or 2,048. The default value is blank.
- **IPSec Certificate Common Name (CN)**: Click **View**to see all the IPSec certificate CNs and their descriptions.
- **Static IP Addresses**: Click **View**to see the static IP addresses of the tenant.

If GRE is enabled and configured for the tenant, you can see the following information:

- Customer IP Address
- Tunnel Name
- Tunnel IP
- Primary Gateway IP
- Secondary Gateway IP
- Managed By

See image.

- **Bypass Authentication for special user agent**: Indicates bypass of authentication for special users who have configured policies for unauthenticated traffic from the ZIA Admin Portal.

- **Nanolog cluster to forward logs from Virtual Service Edge**: This field shows where the tenant's Virtual Service Edge (Virtual ZEN (VZEN)) logs are directed and saved.
- **NSS Subscriptions Multiplier**: This field shows the number of NSS for a tenant. For example, if set to 8, the customer can configure 8 different NSS of each type.

- **API Key**: This field shows the API key used for accessing the public ZIA APIs, if generated.
- **Kerberos password for Virtual Service Edge node(s)**: Indicates whether the password for allowing Kerberos on Virtual Service Edge nodes is enabled or disabled.
- **Extended Bucket Limit in SaaS Security**: Indicates whether an extended bucket limit in SaaS Security scan configuration is enabled or disabled.
- **Large PAC Files (up to 2MB)**: Indicates whether 2MB PAC files are supported or not. The normal limit is up to 256 KB.
- **PAC Files up to 1K**: When enabled, the maximum limit of PAC files per organization is increased to 1,000 (i.e., 1,024 PAC files). When disabled, the maximum number of PAC files allowed per organization is 256.
- **Sandbox API Key Status**: Indicates the access for using the Sandbox APIs.
- **Sandbox API Key**:This field shows the API key used for accessing the Sandbox APIs, if generated.

- **EC API Key**: This field shows the EC API key used for accessing the public EC APIs, if generated.
- **High Group Limit**: Indicates whether the user can belong to more than 100 groups. If enabled, the limit is up to 128.
- **Scheduled Backup**: Indicates whether the user can automate configuration backups from the ZIA Admin Portal.
- **DLP Engine Expansion**: Indicates whether the DLP Engine Expansion is enabled or disabled.
- **DLP Dictionary Expansion**: Indicates whether the DLP Dictionary Expansion is enabled or disabled.

- **Custom EUN for DLP and Cloud App**: When enabled, it shows the End User Notification and Notification Template in the ZIA Admin Portal (Policy > Data Loss Prevention > Add DLP Rule > End User Notification > Notification Template), which allows the customer to link the Zscaler Client Connector notification template to the DLP rules.
- **Enable Digest Authentication**: Indicates whether using a hash instead of a username or password for authenticating is enabled or disabled.

A maximum of 1,024 keyword type identifiers per cloud application instance is allowed. The length of the identifier should not exceed 128 characters.
- **IPv6**: If enabled, this allows seamless connectivity, efficient communication, and large address space to accommodate the increasing number of devices.
- **Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) Labels**: When enabled, it retrieves Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) Labels from the MIP account.
- **Custom Cloud App Support**: When enabled, it allows customers to configure their own applications in the ZIA Admin Portal. This cannot be disabled if any custom cloud applications have been added to a tenant.

- **Authentication Service Admin:**When enabled, it allows admin access to the Authentication Service Admin Portal and the **Managed ZID** link becomes visible. By default, this option is disabled. By default, this option is disabled. Authentication Service is a unified identity service for Zscaler that centralizes and simplifies identity management, user authentication, and entitlement assignment for users to Zscaler services, such as ZIA, ZPA, Multi-Tenant Portal for partners, etc. To learn more, see [Zscaler Authentication Service Help](https://help.zscaler.com/zslogin).

- **AND Functionality for URL Filtering Categories**: When enabled, it provides the support for the logical operation AND between the URL categories in a URL filtering rule in the ZIA Admin Portal. By default, this option is disabled. To learn more, see [Configuring the URL Filtering Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-zia/configuring-url-filtering-policy).
- **Schedule QBR**: This option generates the Quarterly Business Report (QBR) every quarter, if configured.
